Policy: Notification on quality control over the export and import of specific agricultural products (Product Safety and Inspection: 2022/21).
Policy_Content: This Notification lays down the procedures and principles of risk-based quality control over exported and imported agricultural products listed in Annex-I and Annex-II. This Notification shall apply to the exported products that are subject to export regime and inward processing regime as well as to the imported products that are subject to release free for circulation and inward processing regime. This Notification does not cover food safety controls. This Notification sets out provisions on application procedures, inspection, refusal of exported and imported products, secondary inspection, objection against inspection, customs procedures, obligations of the importer and exporter, sampling, analysis, labeling, certification, and sanctions. The company details shall be registered in a database by the Directorate General of Product Safety and Inspection. The quality control of the exported and imported agricultural products listed in Annex-I and Annex-II shall be carried out by the Inspectors in order to assess the compliance to the technical regulations. The criteria for risk analysis shall be established by the Risk Commission.

Policy: Regulation No. 19-T of the Ministry of Natural Resources and Environmental Protection validating Environmental norms and rules.
Policy_Content: These environmental norms and rules establish mandatory rules for conducting an environmental impact assessment. The development of an EIA program is carried out in the form according to the Annex on the basis of: (a) an analysis of alternative technological solutions, taking into account the best available technical methods, their economic efficiency, environmental security, resource consumption per unit of production, the degree of risk and probability of accidents, as well as alternative options placement of the object, including the refusal to place it, taking into account restrictions in the field of environmental protection; and (b) analysis of available information on the current state of the environment, socio-economic and other conditions within the zone of possible impact (materials of topographic survey of the site for the location of the facility, data from the National Environmental Monitoring System in the Republic of Belarus, socio-hygienic monitoring systems, systems for monitoring and forecasting of natural and man-made disasters, data of state cadastres of natural resources, cartographic and aerospace materials, results of sampling and measurements in the field of environmental protection, results of research, development, experimental technological work in relation to the components of the natural environment); and (c) consideration of criteria whether the impact of the proposed economic and other activities may have transboundary effects.
Subject: Environment gen.
Keyword: EIA, Risk assessment/management, Ecofriendly products/ecofriendly processes, Hazards, Transboundary effects, Monitoring, Data collection/reporting, Access-to-information
Geographical_area: CIS (Commonwealth of Independent States), Eastern Europe, Europe, Europe and Central Asia

Policy: Loi N° 2021-034 relative aux contrats de partenariat public-privé.
Policy_Content: La présente loi a pour objet de régir les contrats de partenariat public-privé. Elle détermine leur régime juridique et leur cadre institutionnel. Les contrats de partenariat public-privé, quels que soient leurs montants et sources de financement, satisfont aux principes suivants qui guident l’action publique lors de la préparation, la passation et l’exécution des contrats de partenariat public-privé. Les contrats de partenariat public-privé prennent en compte les objectifs de développement durable dans leurs dimensions environnementale, économique et sociale, en exigeant un contenu local dans les contrats. Les dispositions de la présente loi s’appliquent aux contrats de partenariat public-privé conclus dans tous les secteurs d’activité de la vie économique et sociale sous réserve de l’application de dispositions sectorielles spécifiques ou dérogatoires à la présente loi, applicables aux secteurs des mines, des hydrocarbures, de l’énergie, de l’eau et des télécommunications qui régissent les autorisations, licences et permis octroyés aux partenaires privés.

Policy: Ley Orgánica para la Gestión Integral del Riesgo de Desastres.
Policy_Content: La presente Ley tiene por objeto normar los procesos para la planificación, organización y articulación de políticas y servicios para el conocimiento, prevision, prevención, mitigación; la respuesta y la recuperación ante emergencias, desastres, catástrofes, endemias y pandemias. También regula el funcionamiento del Sistema Nacional Descentralizado de Gestión Integral del Riesgo de Desastres garantizando la seguridad y protección de las personas, las colectividades y la naturaleza, frente a las amenazas de origen natural y antrópico, con el objetivo de reducir el riesgo de desastres. Se crea el Comité Nacional de Reducción de Riesgos; el Comité de Operaciones de Emergencia; el Comité Nacional de Recuperación y Reconstrucción; y la Comisión Técnica Especializada para la Comprensión y el Conocimiento del Riesgo. Se mandata la elaboración de una Política nacional de largo plazo para la gestión integral del riesgo de desastres, la cual tendrá un horizonte temporal de al menos quince años.

Policy: Decree-Law No. 4/2024 establishing the Community Development Planning.
Policy_Content: This Decree-Law establishes the principles and rules that govern Sucos' community development planning. Community development planning is a participatory mechanism for promoting community development, through the involvement of its members in identifying challenges, establishing goals and defining specific strategies and actions, with the aim of improving socio-economic conditions and environmental aspects. Policy: Ley Orgánica para la Igualdad Salarial entre Mujeres y Hombres.
Policy_Content: La presente Ley tiene por objeto garantizar la igualdad de remuneración y cualquier otra forma de retribución económica entre hombre y mujeres en el desempeño de un mismo trabajo o para un trabajo de igual valor. La presente ley tiene por finalidad erradicar prácticas discriminatorias en el ámbito laboral para eliminar la brecha salarial y de remuneración por motivos de género en el ejercicio de las actividades laborales acorde a su relación laboral. Un trabajo se considerará de igual valor a otro cuando la naturaleza de las funciones o tareas efectivamente encame dadas, las condiciones profesionales o de formación exigidas para su ejercicio, los factores estrictamente relacionados con su desempeño y las condiciones laborales en las que dichas actividades se lleven a cabo sean equivalentes.

Policy: Decree-Law No. 2/2024 establishing a special regime for the compensation of individuals whose properties they occupy were expropriated through a declaration of public utility and do not have any title proving ownership and possession of the land.
Policy_Content: This Decree-Law establishes a special regime for the compensation of individuals whose properties they occupy were expropriated through a declaration of public utility and do not have any title proving ownership and possession of the land. It applies to individuals who own urban and rural properties, including rainfed or irrigated properties affected by the implementation and development of projects declared to be of public utility. Owners are considered to be all those who, without having any valid occupation title, are in possession of the property as if they were true owners, without any opposition for at least fifteen years. This special regime also covers occupants who have registered in their favour for more than ten years, benefiting in this case from the presumption of ownership under the terms of article 1265 of the Civil Code, as well as those who have a private purchase and sale or purchase receipt and have been in possession of the property as true owners for more than ten years. Once ownership has been recognized and the beneficiaries of the right to compensation have been determined, the DGPCP sets the value of compensation to be proposed for the land based on the criteria defined in articles 22 et seq. of Legislative Decree No. 3/2007, of 19 July.

Rules for maintaining a register of attributes of generation, provision, circulation and redemption of certificates of origin of electrical energy establish the procedure for maintaining the register of generation attributes, provision, access and redemption of certificates of origin of electrical energy. The register is an ordered collection of data about those registered in the register of qualified generating facilities and their owners, about persons for whom personal accounts have been opened in the registry, about generation attributes and their owners, about certificates of the origin of electrical energy and their owners, as well as operations with generation attributes and certificates recorded in the register.

Policy: Regional Law No. 436-OZ “On the development of responsible business.”
Policy_Content: This Regional Law regulates relations arising between regional government bodies and legal entities in the field of development of responsible business conduct in order to create conditions for ensuring stability, socio-economic and investment development of the region. Responsible business conduct is the activity of responsible organization aimed at improving ecology and environmental protection, using the best available technologies, improving labour conditions of workers, care for employees and members of their families, implementation of environmental, social, educational, charitable and other projects related to improving the standard of living and comfort of the regional population. Authorized regional state executive body shall attribute the status of responsible business entity to businesses meeting the following criteria: (a) environmental impact; (b) use of the best available technologies; (c) promotion of investment projects; and (d) implementation of environmental, social, educational, charitable and other projects related to improving living standards and comfort of the regional population.

Policy: Law No. 24.633 regulating public lands owned by the State, under arts. 246 and 247 of the State Constitution.
Policy_Content: This Law provides for urban and rural public lands owned by the State and their management, collection and allocation, as well as the urban and rural policies referred to in arts. 246 and 247 of the State Constitution. Within the scope of urban and rural policies, the State will promote the preservation of natural and cultural heritage and the rational use of public lands, with the purpose of achieving social justice, observing the competencies established by the State and Federal Constitution. Urban policy aims to enable the sustainable development of the city, taking into account the social function of urbanization, the right to housing and the well-being of its inhabitants and visitors. Rural policy aims to promote sustainable agricultural production, the organization of a healthy food supply and the well-being of workers and rural inhabitants, in order to provide them with the means to settle in the countryside. The allocation of public lands will be compatible with the master plans, the objectives of preserving and protecting the State's natural and cultural heritage, the agricultural policy, the national agrarian reform plan and the Minas Gerais Integrated Development Plan (PMDI).

Policy: Government Decree No. 2323 validating the Rules for organizing the elimination of accumulated environmental damage.
Policy_Content: These Rules establish the procedure for organizing the elimination of accumulated environmental damage, including the performance of the necessary surveys, developing and approving a project for eliminating accumulated damage, the composition of the elimination project, the procedure for monitoring the progress of eliminating accumulated damage and issuing a conclusion. Elimination of accumulated damage is carried out in relation to objects of accumulated damage included in the state register of objects of accumulated environmental damage. The organization of liquidation of accumulated damage in relation to the territory located within the boundaries of land plots owned by a municipality is carried out by local government bodies of such municipality, and in relation to other territories - by state authorities of the constituent entities of the Russian Federation. In cases established by the Government of the Russian Federation, the organization of liquidation of accumulated damage is carried out by the Ministry of Natural Resources and Ecology of the Russian Federation or federal state budgetary institutions subordinate to it, federal state government institutions. Organizing the elimination of accumulated damage includes: (a) conducting the necessary inspections of the facility; (b) development of the liquidation project; (c) approval of the liquidation project; (d) carrying out the elimination of accumulated damage. The contractor carries out the necessary inspections of the facility when developing a liquidation project. Elimination of accumulated damage is carried out by the contractor in accordance with the liquidation project approved by the customer. Monitoring the progress of liquidation of accumulated damage is carried out without any time limit. The object is considered liquidated if there is a conclusion.

Policy_Content: This Regulation establishes the rules for the development and validation of a fire-prevention plan for forests on the territory of a forest management area. The plan for the forest management area is aimed at ensuring implementation of fire prevention measures in forests, substantiation of types, volumes and timing of implementation of fire prevention measures in forests and their priority, to ensure consistency of the above-mentioned measures with other forestry activities in the forest management area, as well as on resource optimization, allocated for forest fire prevention. When developing a plan for a forest management area, it is taken into account potential danger of transition of landscape (natural) fires to forest fund land from adjacent territories. The plan includes a list and scope of forest fire prevention measures and it consists of text and graphic parts. The text part of the plan should include the following sections: (a) a brief description of the forest management area; (b) projected forest fire prevention measures, taking into account the costs of their implementation; (c) the volume and site-by-site distribution of the designed forest fire prevention measures in the context of district forests, indicating the block, division; and (d) calendar plan for the implementation of forest fire prevention measures, part of the plan for forest development in the territory of the forestry district. Graphic part contains maps and schemes. Annex 1 contains the form of fire-prevention plan for forests on the territory of a forest management area.

Policy: Order No. 1174 of the Federal Forestry Agency (ROSLESKHOZ) establishing rates and criteria for the allocation of forest fire control zones.
Policy_Content: Forest fire control zones on forest land are established by executive bodies of the constituent entities of the Russian Federation authorized in the field of forest relations. Control zones are established by written agreement with Federal Forestry Agency (ROSLESKHOZ) for one calendar year no later than February 20 of the corresponding year. The minimum area of a separate section of the control zone established by the executive bodies of the constituent entities of the Russian Federation authorized in the field of forest relations cannot be less than 500 thousand hectares. The location of control zones is allocated quarterly in accordance with the design of forest areas or, in the absence of such, according to characteristic geographical objects (rivers, streams, lake boundaries, watersheds, tops of hills, mountains, ridges). The boundaries of control zones are established in accordance with the quarterly forest management network. The minimum unit for allocating the territory of the control zone is the forest management quarter of the district forestry. If only part of a block falls into the corresponding control zone, regardless of its area, this block entirely belongs to the adjacent forest fire protection zone (airborne detection and ground extinguishing zone, airborne detection and extinguishing zone, exclusive detection zone using space means and predominantly aviation extinguishing).

Policy: Public-Private Partnership Act No. 18 of 2023.
Policy_Content: The Comprehensive Public-Private Partnership Act, comprising 96 articles distributed across eleven Parts, serves as a thorough framework designed to facilitate successful collaborations between the public and private sectors. Its primary objective is to offer guidance on the initiation, administration, and conclusion of such partnerships, prioritizing transparency, accountability, and efficiency. The Act applies to projects executed through the Public-Private Partnership Office - as designated in this legislation, taking the place of the former Public-Private Partnership Unit established under the repealed Act -, and those undertaken under a public-private partnership agreement. It outlines rules and regulations governing the establishment of partnerships between the public and private sectors, covering various aspects such as the tender process, agreement execution, and results publication. Mandating the timely disclosure of tender outcomes and the chosen bidder within fourteen days of executing a public-private partnership agreement, the Act ensures transparency in the process. Additionally, it includes provisions addressing dispute resolution, agreement termination, and delineating the rights and responsibilities of both participating parties. The overarching aim is to foster collaboration between the public and private sectors, enhancing the efficient delivery of projects and services. Through the establishment of clear procedures and requirements, the Act seeks to mitigate risks and enforce accountability in public-private partnerships.

Policy: Order No. 1168 of the Federal Forestry Agency (ROSLESKHOZ) establishing criteria for making a decision on the use of forces and means of the federal state budgetary institution required to carry out work to protect forests from fires in order to implement emergency response measures to forest fires.
Policy_Content: Mandatory criteria shall be as follows: (a) actual involvement of at least 25% of forces of forest fire formations in extinguishing forest fires formations of the authorized executive body of a constituent entity of the Russian Federation exercising powers delegated thereto by the Russian Federation in the field of forest relations included in the consolidated forest fire extinguishing plan on the territory of a constituent entity of the Russian Federation; (b) actual involvement of at least 25% of forces in extinguishing forest fires of no less than 25% of forces of forest fire formations included in the forest fire extinguishing plan on the forestry territory; and (c) presence in a constituent entity of the Russian Federation of at least 10% of forces and means of forest fire formations included in the consolidated forest fire extinguishing plan on the territory of a constituent entity of the Russian Federation, which may be employed in to extinguish forest fires. Additional criteria shall be as follows: (a) detection of a forest fire in the area affected by a forest fire (municipal area) not lower than III class of fire danger in forests, depending on weather conditions according to the Federal Service for Hydrometeorology and Environmental Monitoring, as well as the remote control information system monitoring of the Federal Forestry Agency; (b) availability of forces and means of forest fire formations involved in extinguishing forest fires in the relevant forestry, in respect of which no decision was made to terminate or suspend the work to extinguish them; (c) the presence of an unlocalized forest fire in the forest aviation work area (forest fire area - 100 hectares or more), lasting for more than one day, in respect of which, in accordance with the procedure established by the Rules for extinguishing forest fires, no decision was made to terminate or suspend the work to extinguish it; and (d) the presence of an active forest fire in a 10-kilometer zone from the boundary of a populated area, as well as a protected area of federal significance.

Policy: Government Decree No. 2263 validating the Regulation on response levels to landscape (natural) fires.
Policy_Content: Depending on the time that has passed since receipt of reports of landscape (natural) fires, as well as from other factors affecting the life safety of the population, the following levels of response to landscape (natural) fires are established: (a) municipal level of response to landscape (natural) fires; (b) regional level of response to landscape (natural) fires; and (c) federal level of response to landscape (natural) fires. The municipal level of response is established by decision of the Commission for the Prevention and Elimination of Emergency Situations and ensuring fire safety of the municipality during the emergence of a landscape (natural) fire on the territory of a municipality. If within 24 hours from the receipt of a message about the outbreak of a landscape (natural) the landscape (natural) fire is not localized, proposals on the need to establish a regional level of response (indicating the reasons for the continued spread of landscape (natural) fires) are sent to the commission for the prevention and liquidation of emergency situations and ensuring fire safety of a constituent entity of the Russian Federation: (a) by the head of the directorate of a specially protected area of federal significance in relation to landscape (natural) fires on land of protected areas of federal significance; (b) by the head of the local administration of a municipality in relation to landscape ( natural) fires (with the exception of (natural) fires on forest land, security lands, lands of protected areas). If within 72 hours from the receipt of a message about the outbreak of a landscape (natural) fire, it is not localized, the highest official of the constituent entity of the Russian Federation sends proposals on the need to establish a federal level of response (indicating the reasons for the continued spread of the landscape (natural) fire) to the Federal Forestry Agency - in relation to landscape (natural) fires on forest fund lands, land of protected areas, forest fires on defense and security land. The federal level of response is established before the expiration of 72 hours from the moment a message about a landscape (natural) fire is received by the dispatcher (an official entrusted with the functions of receiving and processing fire messages) of the central fire communications point of the territorial (local) fire and rescue garrison, fire protection department, in the event of a risk of a landscape (natural) fire spreading to a populated area, economic or infrastructure facility and provided there is insufficient forces and means to localize the landscape (natural) fire.

Policy: Law No. 318 of 2023 - Distributed Renewable Energy Production Law.
Policy_Content: This legislation, comprising 12 articles, aims to establish a framework for promoting distributed renewable energy production. It outlines key principles for implementing projects utilizing various forms of net metering (such as individual, multiple-tenants, and collective net metering) and enables peer-to-peer renewable energy trading among private sector entities through direct power purchase agreements and/or leasing of renewable energy equipment. The Law permits private sector entities to trade and sell electricity generated from renewable sources, with a cap of ten megawatts. It applies to distributed renewable energy production under different net metering arrangements and covers both on-site and off-site power purchase agreements for the production and sale of renewable energy. Article 5 addresses the recycling of renewable energy and surplus compensation. Article 6 designates the Electricity Sector Regulatory Authority with the responsibility of monitoring and surveillance, including the development of a database for renewable energy production and conservation in Lebanon. The Electricité du Liban (EDL) is entrusted with overseeing participants, consumers, and producers, and a dedicated Directorate for Renewable Energy will be established within EDL to implement the Law and address related issues.

Policy: Heat Planning and Decarbonization of Heat Networks Law.
Policy_Content: The Law provides for transitioning heat production and supply to renewable energy sources, unavoidable waste heat, or a combination thereof. The primary objective is to contribute to a cost, efficient, sustainable, and greenhouse gas, neutral heat supply by 2045. The law sets a target for 50% of heat in district heating networks to come from renewable energy or waste heat by 2030. It also emphasizes the expansion of district heating networks and the connection of more buildings to these networks. Additionally, the law outlines the involvement of various stakeholders, including producers of renewable energy, gas, and heat, as well as large heat and gas consumers, in the planning process. The law also requires the development of a heat plan, which should include textual, graphical, and cartographic representations of the results of heat planning. It further specifies the involvement of the federal defense ministry and allied military authorities, as well as the evaluation of the availability of green hydrogen and the periodic review of the heat planning process. Furthermore, the law mandates the presentation of an implementation strategy, detailing the steps, timing, costs, responsible parties, and expected positive impacts of the measures to achieve the goals of the law.

Policy: Ley Núm. 21.645 – Modifica el Título II del Libro II del Código del Trabajo "De la protección a la maternidad, paternidad y vida familiar" y regula un régimen de trabajo a distancia y teletrabajo en las condiciones que indica.
Policy_Content: La presente Ley modifica el código del trabajo, introduciendo el derecho al trabajo a distancia o teletrabajo de las personas trabajadoras que desempeñan labores de cuidado no remunerado. Se establece que el empleador deberá ofrecer a la persona trabajadora que, durante la vigencia de la relación laboral, tenga el cuidado personal de un niño o niña menor de catorce años o que tenga a su cargo el cuidado de una persona con discapacidad o en situación de dependencia severa o moderada, no importando la edad de quien se cuida, sin recibir remuneración por dicha actividad, que todo o parte de su jornada diaria o semanal pueda ser desarrollada bajo modalidad de trabajo a distancia o teletrabajo, en la medida que la naturaleza de sus funciones lo permita. La Ley también  busca promover la igualdad de oportunidades y de trato entre las mujeres y hombres, e incluye el reconocimiento de nuevos derechos laborales destinados a favorecer la idea de conciliar la vida familiar. Se establece que los empleadores, teniendo en consideración, en cada caso, la naturaleza de la relación laboral y los servicios prestados, deberán promover el equilibrio entre el trabajo y la vida privada, realizando acciones destinadas a informar, educar y sensibilizar sobre la importancia de la conciliación de la vida personal, familiar y laboral, por medio de campañas de sensibilización y difusión realizadas directamente por el empleador o a través de los organismos administradores de la ley N° 16.744.

Policy: Government Decree No. 2239 validating the Rules for the identification of objects of accumulated environmental damage.
Policy_Content: These Rules establish the procedure for the identification of objects of accumulated environmental damage related to the territories within the boundaries of land plots pertaining to the ownership of municipalities, carried out by local governments of such municipalities and, in relation to other territories, by state authorities of the constituent entities of the Russian Federation. In cases established by the Government of the Russian Federation, identification of objects of accumulated damage is carried out by the Federal Service for Supervision in the Sphere of Environmental Management or federal state budgetary institutions subordinate to this body. Identification of objects of accumulated damage is carried out by state authorities of the constituent entities of the Russian Federation or local government bodies, within a period not exceeding 60 working days from the date of receipt of information, including from state authorities, about the presence of traits of objects of accumulated damage. The collection of information about the territories where economic and other activities were carried out in the past is ensured, inter alia, through: (a) the use of remote monitoring systems (methods); (b) presence of accumulated damage on the territory of the facility; visual inspection of the object of accumulated damage; (c) the use of special technical means that have the functions of photography, audio and video recording, measurement, and other means of collecting or recording information; (d) request to state authorities, local government bodies and organizations related to exchange of interdepartmental information and other interaction for the provision of information; and (e) request from the Unified State Register of Real Estate for an extract about a real estate property containing information about the ownership of objects of accumulated damage and (or) land plots.

Policy: Regional Law No. 105-Z “On apiculture”.
Policy_Content: This Regional Law is aimed at solving the following tasks: (a) creating conditions for breeding, keeping bees, and using them for pollination of agricultural entomophilous plants; (b) development of production of beekeeping products; (c) promoting the protection of bees; and (d) assistance in ensuring compliance with the rights and interests of citizens and legal entities involved in beekeeping. It delimits plenary powers of the Regional Assembly, Regional Government, authorized regional institutions and local government in the field of beekeeping. Terms and conditions of state support of beekeeping envisaged by the federal legislation shall be determined by the Regional Government. The main principles of state support in the field of beekeeping development are: (a) the application procedure for individuals and legal entities engaged in beekeeping for state support; (b) equal access of individuals and legal entities engaged in beekeeping to state support; (c) openness of procedures for providing state support; and (d) provision of state support in compliance with the requirements established by the legislation of the Russian Federation and the legislation of the Republic of Mordovia. A beekeeper, that is, an individual, legal entity or individual entrepreneur operating in the field of beekeeping, has the right: (a) to place stationary apiaries, transportable apiaries for honey collection on land plots owned, leased or used in accordance with the intended purpose and types of permitted use of the land plot, taking into account the veterinary and sanitary requirements established by the legislation of the Russian Federation in the field of veterinary medicine; (b) receive veterinary assistance when carrying out measures to prevent bee diseases, treat them, and control pests of bee colonies; (c) receive from government bodies operating in the fields of environmental protection and veterinary medicine, within their competence, timely, complete and reliable information about the state of the environment, as well as about situations that pose a danger to bees; and (d) demand full compensation for losses caused to him in the manner established by the legislation of the Russian Federation.

Policy: Regional Law No. 260 – PK “On the basics of the formation of ecological culture.”
Policy_Content: This Regional Law, for the purpose of implementing the constitutional rights of citizens of the Russian Federation, establishes the right to a favorable environment, lays down legal and organizational basis for the formation of ecological culture in the regional territory through environmental education and environmental enlightenment. Ecological education is targeted, continuous, unified process of educating and training the population, aimed at the formation of a system of value orientations, moral and ethical standards of behavior, obtaining special knowledge and gaining experience in the field of environmental protection, environmental security and rational use of natural resources. The formation of ecological culture in the region is carried out through environmental education events and environmental enlightenment, an integral part of which is ecological education. The basic principles of the regional state policy in the sphere of formation of ecological culture include: (a) universality, systematicity, complexity and continuity of ecological education and enlightenment; (b) the focus of ecological education on solving practical problems in the conservation and restoration of the environment, resource-saving nature management; (c) openness and accessibility of information about the state of the environment (ecological information); (d) coordination of actions of the regional state bodies, educational organizations, public associations, non-profit organizations, organizations carrying out environmental protection in protected areas of regional significance, and citizens; (e) consideration of the regional characteristics, including natural conditions and resources, environmental situation, demographic situation, cultural and historical traditions of the population, quality of life, intellectual and spiritual potential of the regional population when implementing state policy in the field of formation of ecological culture in the region; and (f) use of historical experience in solving problems of ecological education, as well as the experience of other constituent entities of the Russian Federation and other states.

Policy: Federal Climate Adaptation Act (KAnG).
Policy_Content: The Law aims is to protect life, health, society, economy, infrastructure, nature, and ecosystems by avoiding or largely reducing the negative impacts of climate change, particularly the impending damages. It seeks to enhance the resilience of ecological systems and society to ongoing climate changes to preserve equitable living conditions and contribute to national and international efforts in climate adaptation. Additionally, it aims to prevent the increase of social inequalities due to the adverse effects of climate change. Public authorities are required to consider climate adaptation objectives, particularly concerning floods, droughts, and soil erosion. The Law consists of 14 Articles divided into 5 Parts and discuss about the climate adaptation by the federal government; required considerations; and climate adaptation by the states .

Les eaux de surface, les hydrocarbures liquides et gazeux, ainsi que les schistes bitumineaux font l'objet de lois particulières. L'Etat se réserve le droit d'entreprendre des opérations minières à travers l'organisme public dûment mandaté.

Policy_Content: This Decree approves the Statute of the General Health Inspectorate (IGS), as a national public institution, endowed with legal personality, with technical, administrative and financial autonomy. The IGS carries out inspection and monitoring activities in all areas of healthcare provision, sanitation, disease prevention, maintenance and improvement of Public Health, whether by institutions, services and bodies of the Ministry that oversees the area of health, or by this guardian, or by private entities, natural or legal persons, whether profit-making or non-profit. IGS has the following competencies in the field of Environmental and Occupational Health Inspection: 1. inspect and monitor the sanitary conditions of markets, public spaces and institutions, namely schools, training institutes, boarding schools, daycare and children's centres; 2. monitor the discharge points of sewage networks that may pose a risk to public health; 3. monitor urban solid waste deposit sites and landfills; 4. monitor places where animals are raised, slaughtered and sold for human use and consumption; 5. monitor land for public utility purposes, public buildings, factories and public or private commercial activity, to ensure their maintenance and operation in appropriate conditions; 6. monitor the sanitary conditions of housing, through public complaint, duly instructed; 7. monitor industries or commercial facilities that may cause odors, fluids or noises that pose a risk to public health, etc.

Policy: Federal Law No. 565-FZ “On employment.”
Policy_Content: This Federal Law defines the legal, economic, organizational foundations of state policy in the field of employment, state control over compliance with the legislation on employment. Employment shall be intended labor activity and other activities that do not contradict legislation of the Russian Federation, the activities of citizens, carried out by them for the purpose of producing goods, performing work or provision of services and aimed at generating income. Employed citizens shall be considered the following categories: (a) working under an employment contract, undergoing civil service of the corresponding type, municipal service or having other paid work (service), except for citizens, participating in paid public works, for which the specified jobs are not suitable jobs; (b) individual entrepreneurs; (c) smallholders and indigenous peoples engaged in traditional economic activities; and (d) members of peasant farms. The principles of legal regulation of relations in the sphere of employment of the population are: (a) voluntary work and freedom of choice by citizens of the form of employment, type of activity, profession, specialty, type, nature and mode of work; the lack of employment of citizens cannot serve as a basis for bringing them to administrative or other liability; and (b) ensuring equal opportunities for citizens regardless of gender, race, nationality, language, origin, disability, property and official status, age, place of residence, attitude to religion, beliefs, membership of public associations and other circumstances in the exercise of the right to protection from unemployment and employment promotion.

Policy_Content: This Act consisting of 62 articles and five Schedules aims to promote and regulate investments in Zanzibar. Article 4 establishes the Zanzibar Investment Promotion Authority (ZIPA), a corporate entity having the capacity for legal actions, property transactions, and financial dealings. The functions of the Authority encompass establishing a conducive environment for investment, improving competitiveness, advocating Zanzibar as an appealing investment destination, and exploring investment opportunities. ZIPA is assigned responsibilities like overseeing approved investments, ensuring incentives align with the investor's business plan, and promoting national and international collaboration for streamlined investment activities. In addition, ZIPA manages Special Economic Zones, maintains a register, collaborates with micro, small, and medium enterprises, issues guidelines for corporate social responsibility, and suggests charges for its services. The Authority offers advice to the government on investment-related policies, and monitors incentive schemes. It is also empowered to designate representatives in other countries for implementing its functions. ZIPA shall be managed and administrated by a Board of Directors undertaking functions including (i) formulating and overseeing the implementation of policies; (ii) advising the Minister and relevant government institutions on investment matters; (iii) determining strategies for the Authority's operations; (iv) submitting regular performance reports.

Policy: Government Decree No. 2029 validating the Regulation for the implementation of state monitoring of the state of subsoil and monitoring of the condition of subsoil on a subsoil plot provided for use.
Policy_Content: This Regulation establishes the procedure for the implementation of state monitoring of the state of subsoil and monitoring of the condition of subsoil on a subsoil plot provided for use. State monitoring is a system of regular observations of the state of the subsoil and the processes occurring therein, assessment and forecast of changes in the state of the subsoil under exposure to natural and (or) anthropogenic factors. State monitoring is part of the state environmental monitoring. State authorities of the constituent entities of the Russian Federation when participating in state monitoring, have the right to involve government agencies constituted by the constituent entity of the Russian Federation and (or) contractors under contracts. Federal Agency for Subsoil Management, its territorial bodies and state bodies and institutions subordinate thereto shall carry out state monitoring based on the following data: (a) information obtained as a result of its activities; (b) geological information about the subsoil; (c) information received from other government bodies and their subordinate institutions, government bodies of the constituent entities of the Russian Federation, legal entities and natural persons; and (d) data of the distant zoning of the Earth from outer space. The objectives of state monitoring are: (a) identification, assessment and forecasting of changes in the state of the subsoil under the influence of natural and (or) anthropogenic factors; (b) assessment and forecasting of changes in the state of groundwater; (c) provision of state authorities, local authorities, local self-government, legal entities and natural persons with information about the state of the subsoil and the processes occurring in the subsoil, as well as information on the state of groundwater. State monitoring includes: (a) groundwater monitoring; (b) monitoring of dangerous exogenous geological processes; (c) monitoring of dangerous endogenous geological processes; and (d) monitoring the condition of the subsoil.

Estos incentivos pueden incluir descuentos en impuestos provinciales, acceso a créditos con tasas preferenciales, orden de preferencia en la adjudicación de contratos de obras y servicios públicos, entre otros. Policy: Ley Federal de Protección del Patrimonio Cultural de los Pueblos y Comunidades Indígenas y Afromexicanas.
Policy_Content: La presente Ley tiene por objeto reconocer y garantizar la protección, salvaguardia y el desarrollo del patrimonio cultural y la propiedad intelectual colectiva de los pueblos y comunidades indígenas y afromexicanas. Entre los objetivos, se contempla promover el respeto y desarrollo del patrimonio cultural de los pueblos y comunidades indígenas y afromexicanas, así como reconocer la diversidad de sus elementos; establecer disposiciones para que, en ejercicio de su libre determinación y autonomía, los pueblos y comunidades indígenas y afromexicanas definan, preserven, protejan, controlen y desarrollen los elementos de su patrimonio cultural, sus conocimientos y expresiones culturales tradicionales; establecer las bases para que los pueblos y comunidades indígenas y afromexicanas definan el uso, disfrute y aprovechamiento de su patrimonio cultural y, en su caso, su utilización por terceros; constituir el Sistema de Protección del Patrimonio Cultural de los Pueblos y Comunidades Indígenas y Afromexicanas como mecanismo de coordinación interinstitucional del gobierno federal, conjuntamente con los pueblos y comunidades indígenas y afromexicanas; y establecer las sanciones por la apropiación indebida y el uso, aprovechamiento, comercialización o reproducción del patrimonio cultural, conocimientos y expresiones culturales tradicionales de los pueblos y comunidades indígenas y afromexicanas, según corresponda, cuando no exista el consentimiento libre, previo e informado de dichos pueblos y comunidades o se vulnere su patrimonio cultural.

Policy: Ley 10.934 - Créase la Reserva Provincial de Uso Múltiple Paravachasca.
Policy_Content: En el marco de la Ley N° 6964 (Régimen de Conservación de Áreas Naturales de la Provincia de Córdoba) se crea la Reserva Provincial de Uso Múltiple Paravachasca. Entre los objetivos perseguidos, cabe destacar los siguientes: a) Preservar y asegurar las reservas de agua para sus distintos usos, con especial énfasis para el consumo humano, evitando y previniendo su degradación, contaminación o agotamiento;  b) Establecer mecanismos sustentables y racionales de aprovechamiento de los recursos naturales de la reserva, de modo de satisfacer adecuadamente las necesidades de la región y las poblaciones que la circundan, manteniendo y mejorando su calidad y regularidad; c) Desarrollar programas, planes y acciones tendientes a la conservación, mantenimiento y mejora de las condiciones ambientales, incluyendo al suelo, subsuelo y espacio supra superficial, de modo de coadyuvar al cuidado de los recursos naturales que posee, evitando usos o explotaciones excesivas o inadecuadas; d) Planificar, promover y regular el desarrollo de las actividades antrópicas, de modo tal de reducir al mínimo tolerable o anular las consecuencias nocivas que sobre el ambiente y los recursos hídricos ellas pudieran ocasionar;  e) Potenciar la mejora constante de las condiciones ecológicas de la reserva, propendiendo a la constitución y mejora de un hábitat natural y la vida silvestre que compatibilice el uso de sus recursos, la actividad humana y las condiciones ambientales de modo equilibrado;  f) Establecer limitaciones al dominio, regulación de actividades, ejecución de obras o prestación de servicios a través de los medios legales pertinentes, cuando las circunstancias así lo requieran; g) Fomentar y desarrollar tareas de investigación, educación y estudios en materia hídrica y ambiental, para el más adecuado cumplimiento de los objetivos a los que está destinada; h) Monitorear y vigilar en forma permanente el terreno, previniendo y evitando cualquier acción o hecho degradante, contaminación o actividades humanas nocivas, erosivas, prohibidas o sujetas a limitación, regulación, permiso o autorización de la autoridad, debiendo ésta supervisar su cumplimiento en las condiciones acordadas.

Policy: Order No. 760 of the Ministry of Natural Resources and Ecology validating federal rules and regulations in the field of hydrometeorology and related areas, establishing mandatory requirements for the organization and conduct of work on active impact on hydrometeorological processes (fog dispersal).
Policy_Content: These federal rules and regulations establish mandatory requirements for the organization and conduct of fog dispersal work using methods of active impact on hydrometeorological processes. Fog dispersal work is carried out by legal entities that are specialized organizations for active impact on hydrometeorological processes, on the basis of a license to carry out work on active impact on hydrometeorological processes, issued by the Federal Service for Hydrometeorology and Environmental Monitoring. The purpose of fog dispersal work is to increase the visibility range on roads and airfields through deliberate changes in the natural course of fog evolution in the desired direction (changes in the physical properties of the environment in a given part of the surface layer of the atmosphere). Fog dispersal work is carried out using active means. When predicting the appearance of fog, it is necessary to put equipment in full readiness, fill containers with liquid nitrogen, and continuously monitor the parameters of the ground layer: air temperature, temperature profile, wind speed and direction, visibility range.

Policy: Law No. 1993 “On apiculture.”
Policy_Content: This Law establishes the legal, organizational and economic basis for carrying out activities in the field of apiculture, the directions and procedure for state regulation, as well as guarantees for the protection of property rights in this sector, aimed at protecting and increasing bee colonies, manufactured products and the effective use of honey bees in the pollination of entomophilous plants. Natural persons and legal entities freely carry out entrepreneurial activities in the field of apiculture in the manner established by the legislation of the Republic of Tajikistan. Business entities in the field of apiculture may create unions (associations) and (or) become members of them in the manner determined by the national legislation. Natural persons who are not individual entrepreneurs are authorized to carry out activities in the field of apiculture to meet their own personal needs in the amount of up to 30 bee families. Ready and (or) prepared apiculture products are sold after passing a veterinary and sanitary examination for compliance with food safety requirements and in the presence of a document confirming the quality and safety of the products. Natural persons and economic entities in the apiculture sector, organize apiaries with equipment, tools and other necessary material resources on the relevant land plots. The apiary is organized on the basis of a zoning plan for honey bee breeds in the relevant zones. Local executive bodies of state power have the right to establish the number of apiaries placed by natural persons and business entities in the field of apiculture within the boundaries of suburban and green zones, based on the conditions of keeping honey bees and in accordance with veterinary and sanitary norms and rules. The procedure for placing hives with bee families on the territory of horticultural and gardening organizations is determined by the general meeting of these organizations. Registration of apiaries is carried out on the basis of a veterinary and sanitary certificate issued by the authorized state body in the field of food safety. Individuals and legal entities engaged in the cultivation of entomophilous plants, in order to increase their productivity, can use bee colonies that are their own and (or) the property of other persons. Prevention of diseases of honey bees, their treatment and control of harmful insects are carried out in accordance with the veterinary legislation of the Republic of Tajikistan. Natural persons and business entities in the sector of apiculture are responsible for the implementation of measures to prevent diseases of honey bees, including diseases inserted by the authorized state body in the field of food safety in the list of particularly dangerous diseases, their treatment and the fight against pests of bee colonies. This Law contains 6 Chapters divided into 30 Articles. Chapter 1 lays down general provisions. Chapter 2 establishes the activities in the field of apiculture. Chapter 3 regards state regulation in the field of apiculture. Chapter 4 regards ownership in the field of apiculture. Chapter 5 regards protection of honeybees. Chapter 6 lays down final provisions.

Policy_Content: This Decree-Law establishes the Ministry of Commerce and Industry (MCI). Las personas naturales, al solicitar el arrendamiento de equipos agropecuarios, demuestran las actividades económicas que realizan vinculadas a las producciones agropecuarias, azucareras y forestales con la presentación de los siguientes documentos: a) Certificado de tenedor inscripto de tierra o resolución del delegado municipal de la Agricultura reconociéndolo como productor agropecuario; b) contrato laboral; c) licencia como trabajador por cuenta propia para actividades agropecuarias; y d) otras que correspondan. Policy_Content: This Presidential Regulation concerns the allocation of land for the arrangement of investment in the sectors of mining, plantation, and forest utilisation. Policy: Presidential Regulation no. 62 of 2023 concerning the Acceleration of Implementation of Agrarian Reform.
Policy_Content: This Presidential Regulation provides for strengthening the implementation of the agrarian reform, as a national strategic program to create justice in land ownership and management, to improve land distribution, and to resolve agrarian conflicts. According to the Regulation, the agrarian reform provides for achieving a fair and prosperous society, through the redistribution of land, the legalisation of assets, and the implementation of targeted strategies and programmes. The Regulation focuses on the following objects of the agrarian reform: the land controlled by the State, the land owned or utilised by the local communities, for redistribution or legalisation purposes. Policy: Order No. 631 of the Ministry of Natural Resources and Ecology validating the Procedure for assigning numbers to a forestry (district forestry), forest quarter, forest taxation unit, forest plot, cutting area, information about which is included in the state forest register.
Policy_Content: This Order establishes the Procedure for assigning numbers to a forestry (district forestry), forest quarter, forest taxation unit, forest plot, cutting area, information about which is included in the state forest register. Registration numbers for forest districts (district forestry), forest quarter, forest taxation units, forest plots, cutting areas, information about which is entered into the state forest register, are assigned by the federal executive body authorized to maintain the state forest register. Accounting numbers for forest districts (district forestry), forest quarters, forest taxation units, forest plots, cutting areas are assigned in the federal state information system of the forestry complex when information about forest districts (district forestry), forest quarters, forest taxation units, forest plots, cutting areas is entered into the state forest register in the manner prescribed by the Rules for maintaining the state forest register. An accounting number is assigned to a forestry area depending on its full or partial location on the territory of a constituent entity of the Russian Federation. If the forestry is located on the territory of several constituent entities of the Russian Federation, the registration number of the forestry consists of the numbers “00”, a separator in the form of a colon and the serial number of the forestry located on the territory of several constituent entities of the Russian Federation. The registration number for a district forestry is assigned to the forestry within the boundaries of which such a district forestry is located. An accounting number for a forest quarter is assigned to the district forestry within which boundaries such a forest quarter is located. An accounting number is assigned to a forest taxation unit in the forest quarter within the boundaries of which such a forest taxation unit is located. The registration number for a forest plot is assigned to the forestry within which boundaries such a forest plot is located. The registration number for a cutting area is assigned to the forest plot within the boundaries of which such a cutting area is located.

The period of validity of the exclusive license for the export of certain types of fertilizers is one year from the start date and may be limited within the validity period of a foreign trade agreement (contract) or document that is the basis for issuing an exclusive license. The licensor decides to suspend the exclusive license in the following cases: (a) voluntary application of the licensee; (b) suspension of one or more documents on the basis of which the exclusive license was issued; (c) failure by licensees to submit quarterly, before the fifteenth day of the month following the reporting quarter, a report on the progress of execution of the exclusive license to the licensor; (d) licensees indicate false information in quarterly reports on the progress of execution of the exclusive license; and (e) the presence of a judicial act.

Policy: Regulation (EU) 2023/1805 on the use of renewable and low-carbon fuels in maritime transport, and amending Directive 2009/16/EC.

Policy: Ministerial Decree of 5 September 2023 concerning interventions for the agri-food chain.
Policy_Content: The Decree defines terms and sets out provisions related to the protection of agricultural products with DOP and IGP designations. In particular it defines eligibility criteria to access the «Fund» (Fund for the development and support of supply chains agricultural, fishing and aquaculture, established by art. 1, paragraph 128, of Law No. 178/2020). Beneficiaries eligible for contributions include consortia for protection and temporary associations among them. The activities and eligible expenses include information campaigns, public relations, participation in fairs, and development costs to improve product sustainability. The decree specifies contribution types, amounts, the possibility of advance payments, and compliance with state aid regulations. Detailed requirements for beneficiaries and implementation details are delegated to a subsequent ministerial provision.
Subject: Agricultural & rural development
Keyword: Agricultural development, Special fund, Cooperative/producer organization

Policy: Resolution No. 88/2021 approving the Investment Directives for the Environment for the period 2021-2025.
Policy_Content: This Resolution, consisting of 8 articles and three Annexes, approves the Investment Directives for the Environment for the period 2021-2025. The Environment Fund is an important instrument for implementing the country's environmental policy. This Resolution approves the Investment Directives for the Environment relating to the periods from: a) 2021-2024 for municipal projects; and b) 2021-2025 for programmes and projects of the Central Administration and those presented by companies and civil society organizations. For the period 2021-2024, municipal projects that fall under the Multi-Year Public Investment Plan in the following areas are eligible for financing from the Environment Fund: a) Integrated management of urban solid waste; b) Environmental awareness; c) Basic Sanitation; and d) Animal Health. For the period 2021-2025, projects submitted by the Central Administration that fall under the Multi-Year Public Investment Plan in the following areas are eligible for financing from the Environment Fund: a) Basic sanitation; b) Integrated management of waste and hazardous products; c) Prevention of different forms of environmental pollution and environmental degradation and restoration of ecosystems; d) Wildlife protection; e) Recovery of Degraded Forest Areas; f) Environmental awareness; g) Strategic and action planning in the field of the Environment; and h) Environmental statistics and information.

Policy: Decree-Law No. 54/2023 on the Ministry of Social Solidarity and Inclusion.
Policy_Content: This Decree-Law approves the Ministry of Social Solidarity and Inclusion (MSSI). MSSI is the government department responsible for the design, execution, coordination and evaluation of the policy, defined and approved by the Council of Ministers, for the areas of social security, social assistance and community reintegration, ensuring the implementation of the gender integrated approach policy in all social protection programmes developed by MSSI. The MSSI's responsibilities are: a) Design and implement social security systems for workers and the rest of the population; b) Develop social assistance programmes; c) Promote humanitarian aid to the most disadvantaged; d) Propose and develop policies and strategies for managing disaster risks with social impact; e) Develop and implement social assistance programmes in disaster risk management, namely in emergency response and post-disaster recovery, in coordination with relevant institutions; f) Provide monitoring, protection and community reintegration of vulnerable groups, including people with special needs and disabilities (EHD); g) Establish collaboration and coordination mechanisms with other Government bodies responsible for related areas.

Policy: The Climate Change (Amendment) Act, no. 9 of 2023.
Policy_Content: This Act provides for amending the 2016 Climate Change Act, by introducing new definitions, and replacing sections. This Act defines: aggregate earnings, as total of all income in a carbon project; carbon budget, as the approved quantity of greenhouse gas emission that is acceptable over a specified time; carbon credits; carbon market; carbon project; carbon offset; carbon standards; community; mitigation outcomes; nature-based solutions; non-market approaches; reduced emissions from deforestation and forest degradation; share of proceeds, as the levies from activities under the Paris Agreement, used to cover administrative expenses. Amendments concern: guidance in the development and implementation of carbon markets; reviewing and recommending the level of compliance with international climate commitments; identification of past, current and projected sector-based greenhouse gases emission profile; insertion of a new Part focusing on the regulation of carbon markets, including: trade in carbon markets; participation in carbon markets, as a result of a bilateral or multilateral trading agreement; promoting the mitigation of greenhouse gas emissions, while fostering sustainable development; environmental impact assessment; provision of social and environmental benefits; public land-use projects; dispute resolution; fees; offences and penalties.

Policy: Order No. 322 of the Minister of Agriculture of the Republic of Kazakhstan validating the Regulation for crediting projects in the agricultural sector.
Policy_Content: This Regulation establishes the procedure for crediting projects in the agricultural sector performed by natural persona and legal entities. Credits are provided to applicants to create new or expand existing projects in the agricultural sector from the national budget and/or local budgets. Loans issued for the implementation of projects in the agricultural sector are provided through an attorney (agent). The local executive body provides budget loan funds under a contract of entrustment to an attorney (agent) in accordance with the budget and civil legislation of the Republic of Kazakhstan. It establishes the maximum period for repayment of credit (10 years) and the maximum credit sum (5 billion tenge). The intended purpose of the credit is the implementation of projects in the agricultural sector aimed at creating new ones or expanding existing facilities in the following fields: (a) dairy farms (capacity from 400 heads); (b) poultry farms for meat production (from 5000 tons of poultry meat per year); (c) vegetable storage facilities (from 1000 tons); and (d) irrigated agriculture (potatoes and vegetables, feed production) using modern water saving technologies (sprinkling, drip irrigation).

Policy: Executive Decree No. 186/23 approving the Statute of the Women's Professional Training Centre.
Policy_Content: This Executive Decree, approves the Statute of the Women's Professional Training Centre. This Statute establishes the general rules for the organization and operation of the Women's Professional Training Centre, as an indirect executive service of the National Institution of Employment and Professional Training, dedicated to carrying out professional training activities. This Centre is subject to the direction, administrative organization, supervision, methodological and technical guidance of the National Institution of Employment and Professional Training. The Women's Professional Training Centre has the following responsibilities: a) Carry out professional training activities, in accordance with the requirements of the National Professional Training System (SNFP); b) Promote the appreciation of trainees, providing them with technical knowledge, in order to allow them to quickly enter the job market; c) Collaborate in identifying local needs for training and professional rehabilitation actions; d) Promote adjustment between demand, supply and professional training; e) Provide job search support services; f) Collaborate, with other public and private services, in collecting information on the employment and professional training market; g) Intermediate labour with the aim of placing the unemployed in the job market, through vacancies obtained from employers; h) Collaborate in the implementation of measures included in active employment policies; i) Facilitate professional guidance based on job market offers; j) Promote equal opportunities in employment and professional training, etc.

Policy: Decree No. 52/2023 approving the Regulation on Quality Standards for Water Discharge of Liquid and Solid Effluents.
Policy_Content: This Regulation establishes the quality standards of non-treated water and effluent discharge, establishing the maximum permissible concentration levels of pollutants in surface and underground water resources. The Regulation applies to all public and private entities that carry out activities within the national territory, which can directly or indirectly modify the quality of water, through discharges of effluents. The operation of discharging effluents into surface and underground water resources, with standards different from those established in Annex II of this Regulation, is subject to authorization by the Regional Water Administration, Public Institution (ARA, IP) of the respective area of jurisdiction, upon opinion from the entity that oversees the environmental area. Water quality standards at their acceptable level that do not have a significant impact on a given water course are those established in Annex II. The discharge of industrial, agricultural, livestock, domestic effluents, urban, suburban and mineral rainwater must comply with the water quality standards established in Annex II.

Policy: Law on freedom of access to information at the level of Bosnia and Herzegovina institutions.
Policy_Content: This Law here determines the right to access information and reuse documents in the possession of the government institutions of Bosnia and Herzegovina, legal entities that establish institutions of Bosnia and Herzegovina in accordance with the provisions of the Law on registration of legal entities that establish institutions of Bosnia and Herzegovina (Official Gazette of BiH 37/2003 and 76/2011) and independent bodies of Bosnia and Herzegovina established by special laws. The aim of this Law is to enable and ensure the realization of the right to free access to information for natural and legal persons, through the openness and publicity of the activities of BiH institutions, in accordance with international treaties on human rights and freedoms and generally accepted rules of international law, this and other laws, in order to achieve and protection of public interests and realization of free and democratic order and open society. All information of BiH institutions is considered open and public, unless the non-publication is fully justified and based on exceptions prescribed by specific law.

Policy: Bylaw No. 57 of 2023  to compensate farmers affected by agricultural risks issued pursuant to Paragraph (C) of Article 4 of the Agricultural Risk Management Fund Law No. 5 of 2009.
Policy_Content: These Regulations consisting of 13 articles aim to compensate farmers who are non-subscribers in the fund. The system also seeks to address the Kingdom’s vulnerability to climate change and emergence of natural hazards, primarily torrential rains and winds that affect crops more than frost risk. In particular they establish at article 3 that (i) the compensation requested is limited to the injured party; (ii) it is not permissible to compensate the victim for damage caused by agricultural risks on the farm more than once during the agricultural season. The required conditions for the affected farmers' loan request to be accepted are dealt with in Article 4. Under article 5 a Compensation Committee is formed in the Fund, headed by the Secretary-General of the Ministry and with membership of officials who are experts in the field of agriculture, animal breeding and plant cultivation. The main functions of the Committee are listes in article 6 as follows (i) review the reports presented by the inspection committees established under the provisions of this system, and endorse the accompanying reports and statements; (ii) evaluate compensation appeals and objections from individuals impacted by agricultural risks, forwarding recommendations to the Fund’s Affairs Management Committee for appropriate decision-making; (iii) propose compensation rates for affected parties based on the cost and revenue guidelines sanctioned by the Fund Management Committee. The Minister forms a committee in the relevant Agriculture Directorate called the Damage Investigation Committee with the main task of inspecting and report about the affected farms.

Policy: Decreto Nº 1384 - Por el cual se reglamenta el capítulo IV y las demás disposiciones ambientales contenidas en la Ley 70 de 1993, en lo relacionado con los recursos naturales renovables y del ambiente, en los territorios colectivos adjudicados, en trámite u ocupados ancestral y/o tradicionalmente por las comunidades negras, afrocolombianas, raizales y palenqueras, y se adiciona al Título 12 de la Parte 2 del Libro 2 del Decreto 1076 de 2015 - Decreto Único Reglamentario del Sector Administrativo del Sector Ambiente y Desarrollo Sostenible y se dictan otras disposiciones.
Policy_Content: Por medio del presente se dispone a reglamentar el Capítulo IV y las demás disposiciones ambientales contenidas en la Ley 70 de 1993, en lo relacionado con el uso de la tierra, la protección, y el aprovechamiento de los recursos naturales renovables y del ambiente, en los territorios colectivos de las comunidades negras, afrocolombianas, raizales y palenqueras del país. El ámbito de aplicación del Decreto son las comunidades negras, afrocolombianas, raizales y palenqueras que habitan en todo el territorio nacional en los territorios colectivos. El principal instrumento para ejercer la gobernanza en los territorios colectivos serán los planes de etnodesarrollo. Los planes de manejo ambiental de los territorios colectivos será el mecanismo propio de gobierno y manejo del territorio colectivo, que adopta el Consejo Comunitario, como un instrumento de planificación del uso, manejo y administración ambiental del territorio y de los recursos naturales renovables. Los bosques de las comunidades negras, afrocolombianas, raizales y palenqueras, tienen el carácter de propiedad colectiva y sus titulares son las comunidades beneficiarias de la titulación colectiva. Las autoridades ambientales podrán constituir y delimitar, reservas naturales especiales dentro de los territorios adjudicados de las comunidades negras, afrocolombianas, raizales y palenqueras. Las prácticas tradicionales que las comunidades ejerzan sobre las fuentes hídricas localizadas en sus territorios colectivos tendrán prelación sobre los demás usos y aprovechamientos que otros ejerzan sobre estas fuentes hídricas. Se ordena al Ministerio de Ambiente y Desarrollo Sostenible a formular y adoptar la política para la protección de los sistemas de conocimientos tradicionales y saberes ancestrales asociados a la biodiversidad, en el marco de sus competencias y a los lineamientos del Convenio internacional de Diversidad Biológica.

Policy_Content: El objeto del presente Decreto es Reglamentar el Capítulo V de la Ley 70 de 1993 y adoptar mecanismos especiales para el fomento y desarrollo de las actividades mineras por parte de las comunidades negras, afrocolombianas, raizales y palenqueras en territorios colectivos, territorios en trámite de adjudicación y ocupados ancestralmente por estas comunidades. El Consejo Comunitario ejercerá ante la autoridad minera competente las funciones que se señalan en el Artículo 2.2.5.11.1.1. Dentro de los territorios colectivos, la autoridad minera competente podrá delimitar zonas mineras en las cuales la exploración y explotación de los recursos naturales no renovables, se realice por parte de las comunidades y bajo condiciones técnicas especiales, con el fin de preservar sus características económicas y culturales. Se regula el derecho de prelación para la exploración, explotación y aprovechamiento de los recursos naturales no renovables. La Licencia Especial de Exploración y Explotación de recursos naturales no renovables en los territorios colectivos se otorgará por parte de la autoridad minera competente, mediante un Contrato de Concesión Minera Especial, el cual se regirá por los requisitos diferenciales que se establecen en el presente Decreto.

Policy: Law No. 13/2023 approving the Law on Labour.
Policy_Content: This Law defines the general principles and establishes the legal regime applicable to individual and collective relationships of subordinate work, provided for hire and for remuneration. It applies to legal relationships of subordinate employment established between employer and worker, national and foreign, from all fields of activity, who carry out their activity in the Country. This Law also applies to legal employment relationships established between public legal entities and their employees, who are not State employees or whose relationship is not regulated by specific legislation. The Law also applies to associations, non-governmental organizations, the cooperative sector, with regard to salaried workers, diplomatic and consular missions in relation to locally hired workers, international organizations and other natural or legal persons of Private Law. Workers are guaranteed equal rights at work, regardless of their ethnic origin, place of birth, language, color, race, sex, gender, marital status, age, within the limits established by law, social status, religious or political ideas. The female worker is guaranteed, during the period of pregnancy and after giving birth, the following rights: a) not to carry out, without reduction in remuneration, work that is clinically inadvisable due to her state of pregnancy; b) not perform night work or be transferred from their usual place of work, from the third month of pregnancy; c) interrupt daily work to breastfeed the child; d) not terminate the employment contract during pregnancy up to one year after the end of the leave.

Policy_Content: This Decree creates the Partnership Management System (Sigpar) with a view to organizing the activities of planning, coordination, guidance and management of partnerships for the implementation of public policies in a decentralized manner, within the scope of the bodies and entities of the federal public administration. Sigpar covers the bodies and entities of the direct Federal administration and the dependent state companies responsible for planning, formalizing, celebrating, monitoring and evaluating related partnerships. Sigpar comprises the following forms of partnerships that involve mutual collaboration and public and mutual interest: I - transfer of financial resources; II - decentralization of budget credits; III - acquisition and donation of material goods or services; IV - execution of funds arising from tax waiver; and V - cooperation free of charge, without transferring Union resources or assets. Policy_Content: This Administrative Regulation defines the procedure for providing public services for issuing and re-registration of environmental auditor's qualification certificate. Services for issuing and re-registration of the qualification certificate are provided through the state services center or the Unified interactive state services portal of the Republic of Uzbekistan. The candidate applies to the state service center directly or through a trusted representative to use the state services for the issuance of the certificate of qualification, or registers for the use of state services in electronic form at the National Institute of Education and Culture. Regulation on the procedure for maintaining the register of environmental audit organizations determines the procedure for forming and maintaining the Register of Environmental Audit Organizations. Environmental audit organization shall be intended a legal entity that performs environmental audit activities. Entry into the register is carried out free of charge by the authorized body. The main tasks of creating and maintaining the register are as follows: (a) forming a list of environmental audit organizations and providing electronic access to information about them for interested persons; (b) creation of a single electronic database of information on the provision of environmental audit services by environmental audit organizations; (c) systematic collection of information on the status and potential of environmental audit organizations; and (d) creating the possibility of conducting monitoring of information on the compliance of environmental audit organizations with the requirements established by legislation.
