Policy: Presidential Decree No. UP-85 “On additional measures to support household farming in the field of cocoons and further expand the food base for growing cocoons”.
Policy_Content: The President, in order to further develop homework in the care of silkworms in the country, create clusters and farms in the field of sericulture and mulberry growing, as well as households specializing in growing silkworms, by creating new mulberry plantations through the development of rainfed lands and pastures, as well as further expansion feed base for the cultivation of silkworm raw materials, decrees as follows: (a) starting from June 2023, based on the proposals of the Ministry of Agriculture, the Committee for the Development of the Silk and Wool Industry under the Ministry of Agriculture, the Council of Ministers of the Republic of Karakalpakstan and local self-government (regional khokimiyats), create in the regions: new sericulture clusters involved in silkworm care, procurement, processing of grown raw silk, creation of a value chain, direction to the domestic market and export of finished products; (b) new farms in the field of sericulture and mulberry growing, growing mulberry seedlings, creating mulberry plantations, caring for silkworms, harvesting raw silk; (c) the Council of Ministers of the Republic of Karakalpakstan and the local self-government (khokimiyats of the regions), together with the Ministry of Agriculture, within two weeks, to allocate to the Committee land plots on the right of permanent use with a clear definition of their contours for the creation of new mulberry plantations by sericulture clusters, farms in the direction of sericulture and mulberry growing in accordance with Appendix No. 1; (c) to stablish that land plots for the creation of new mulberry plantations with a size of at least 10 hectares are allocated to sericulture clusters, farms in the field of sericulture and mulberry growing, as an exception, on a leasehold basis in accordance with an investment agreement or a public-private partnership agreement concluded with the Committee; (d) the Committee, the Uzbekipaksanoat Association, the Council of Ministers of the Republic of Karakalpakstan, local self-government (regional khokimiyats), when creating sericulture clusters, farms in the field of sericulture and mulberry growing, are responsible for the selection and formation of potential legal entities that carry out economically sustainable activities, have the necessary infrastructure facilities, as well as property and other assets; (e) the Ministry of Agriculture, together with the Committee and the Uzbekipaksanoat Association, within two months, develop and submit to the Cabinet of Ministers a procedure for leasing land plots for creating new mulberry plantations to sericulture clusters, farms in the field of sericulture and mulberry growing in accordance with an investment agreement or an agreement on public -private partnership; (f) to approve the forecast indicators for the creation of new mulberry plantations on land allocated to the Committee for the Development of the Silk and Wool Industry under the Ministry of Agriculture in 2023-2027 on the right of permanent use, in accordance with Appendix No. 2; (g) the Council of Ministers of the Republic of Karakalpakstan and the local self-government (khokimiyats of the regions), based on the need of each territory for the creation of mulberry plantations, take measures to allocate land plots to mulberry farms in the prescribed manner for harvesting seeds and seedlings of mulberry in the prescribed amount; (h) to determine, according to the proposals of the Ministry of Agriculture, the Committee and the Uzbekipaksanoat Association, the area of mulberry plantations belonging to the territorial limited liability companies "Agropilla" and attached to the population on the basis of a family contract, in the amount of 0.5 hectares to 2 hectares; (i) to authorize to plant vegetables, potatoes, gourds, flowers, herbs and medicinal plants, corn, legumes and oilseeds in the aisles of mulberry trees on a land plot attached to sericulture households;(j) the Agency for the Work of Mahallabai and Entrepreneurship Development under the Ministry of Employment and Poverty Reduction, as well as assistants to local self-government (khokims of districts (cities) are personally responsible for ensuring employment of the population by organizing the activities of sericulture households on the terms of a family contract; and (j) silkworm grits and resources for caring for them, including bedding paper, thermometer, plastic wrap, psychrometer (for hatcheries) and other necessary resources, shall be provided free of charge by sericulture clusters to homeworkers, sericulture households, sericulture farms and farms in the field of sericulture.

Policy: Presidential Decree No. PP-73 “On measures for the further development of silk industry”.

This Presidential Decree establishes that commercial banks allocate revolving loans to enterprises exporting silk products for their continuous provision of working capital for a period of 3 years at a rate of 5 percent per annum (with a bank margin not exceeding 1 percent). It also establishes the procedure in accordance with which, within the framework of the sources of subsidy financing, enterprises for the processing of cocoons and the production of silkworm cocoons are allocated from the national budget a subsidy in the amount of 120 thousand soums for each box of silkworm grenae supplied by them directly to persons involved in the cultivation of silkworm cocoons . It approves the proposal of silk industry enterprises to assign silk industry enterprises to local self-government in accordance with the Annex in order to ensure the employment of citizens, fulfillment of forecasts and organized conduct of the silkworm growing season, as well as providing ongoing practical assistance to industry enterprises. The Ministry of Investment, Industry and Trade, starting from March 1, 2023, will simplify the procedure for the export of raw silk in order to create favorable conditions for business entities in the export of silk products and prevent bureaucratic obstacles in this field.

Policy: Presidential Decree No. PP-171 “On measures to effectively organize the activities of the Ministry of Ecology, Environmental Protection and Climate Change”.
Policy_Content: Priority areas of activity of the Ministry of Ecology, Environmental Protection and Climate Change are: (a) development and implementation of a unified state policy in the field of nature conservation, rational use and restoration natural resources, waste management, and climate change; (b) conducting state environmental control for the protection of nature, including atmospheric air, lands, bowels, waters, forests, protected natural areas, protection of wild fauna and wild flora, waste management; (c) ensuring the protection, conservation, of forests, afforestation and reforestation, increasing the productivity and rational use of forests; (d) organization of hydrometeorological service, monitoring of climate change and environmental pollution; (e) development of cooperation with civil society institutions and the public in the field of nature protection, system organization environmental education and support of scientific research; (f) introduction of the principles of "green” development, reduction of harmful emissions into the environment, reducing the negative impact of human activities on nature; (g) introduction of digital technologies in the field of nature protection, establishing a system for reducing and automating the human factors in monitoring; (h) further development of ecotourism, hunting and safari tourism, effective use of forestry opportunities and national natural parks (with the exception of areas transformed into nature reserves) and the construction of appropriate infrastructure facilities, creation of favorable conditions for foreign and domestic tourists and provision of their services; (i) application of effective measures to prevent, detect and suppress violation of the requirements of legislation in the field of protection nature and rational use of natural resources; (j) monitoring the state of the environment, identifying factors that can lead to environmental pollution, irrational use of natural resources, creating risks to life and health of citizens; (k) monitoring the compliance of the ongoing economic and other activities standards, norms, rules for nature protection and the requirements of other regulatory legal acts, as well as application of legal measures; (l) ensuring the observance of the rights and legitimate interests of legal persons and individuals, fulfilling their duties in the field of nature protection and rational use of natural resources; and (m) establishing control over the rational use of forests, regulation of relations in the field of nature protection, control over organization of ground and aerial protection of forests.

Policy: Presidential Decree No. UP-81 “On measures to transform the field of ecology and environmental protection and organize the activities of the authorized state body”.
Policy_Content: The President, considering the new tasks and functions assigned by this Decree, orders to rename the Ministry of Natural Resources into the Ministry of Ecology, Environmental Protection and Climate Change. This Presidential Decree introduces from July 1, 2023 in the Republic of Uzbekistan the system of "Public environmental control" and determines the rights and obligations of controllers as follows: (a) identification of environmental offenses, execution and inclusion in the Environmental Control Platform of the relevant act; (b) receiving free education and advanced training in order to acquire special knowledge and skills in the implementation of activities; (c) obtaining information on the measures taken in relation to the identified offenses, participation in the processes related to the sentencing of the offender; and (d) receiving remuneration for efficient activities in the manner and in the amount established by law. Public environmental controllers are required to ensure transparency, counteract corruption, as well as objectively prepare reliable data in the process of identifying and reporting offences. Inspectorate of state environmental control without the status of a separate legal entity shall be set up within the structure of the Ministry of state environmental control. Inspection in its activities is subordinated to and accountable to the Minister of Ecology, Environmental Protection and Climate Change – Chief state environmental inspector. Treatment of municipal solid waste in the country shall be carried out through a new procedure and mechanisms based on the principles of "zero waste" (Zero waste). In doing so, special attention shall be paid to: (a) separate collection and disposal of waste depending on the types of household waste; (b) processing (recycling) or incineration at the maximum level of newly generated waste without sending it to landfills, introducing it into the sphere of circular economy practice; (c) ensuring the phased complete processing and incineration of waste at all operating landfills; (d) directing excess heat or electricity generated as a result of waste incineration to meet the needs of the population and production on existing energy and communication networks as payment, including using the "green tariff"; and (e) introduction of a system for allocating "green subsidies" from the State budget in order to increase the efficiency of this system.

In particular, in order to implement international norms into national legislation, apply new approaches to solving problems arising from technical and technological processes in the field of environmental protection, as well as actively participate in the efforts of the international community aimed at maintaining a safe level of the environment and combating climate change, the Republic of Uzbekistan becomes a party to new international treaties and a member of international organizations. The President takes note that: (a) in accordance with the Law of the Republic of Uzbekistan “On ratification of the Stockholm Convention on Persistent Organic Pollutants (Stockholm, May 22, 2001)”, the Republic of Uzbekistan ratified the Stockholm Convention on Persistent Organic Pollutants; (b) the Republic of Uzbekistan became a member of the International Union for Conservation of Nature on October 20, 2021; and (c) in accordance with the requirements of international treaties and international organizations, the Republic of Uzbekistan has assumed the obligation to pay membership fees.

Policy: Governmental Decree No. 881 validating the Regulation on calculating and collecting fees for negative environmental impact and on recognizing as invalid some acts of the Government of the Russian Federation and a separate provision of an act of the Government of the Russian Federation.
Policy_Content: Regulation on calculating and collecting fees for negative environmental impact and exercising control for the correctness of its calculation, completeness and timeliness of its payment, as well as the calculation of quarterly advance payments. Negative impact fees are calculated and collected for the following types of negative impact on the environment: (a) emissions of pollutants into the atmospheric air from stationary sources; (b) discharges of pollutants into waterbodies; and (c) storage, disposal of production and consumption waste, including storage of industrial by-products recognized as waste. Payment for the negative impact must be made by legal persons and individual entrepreneurs engaged on the territory of the Russian Federation, the continental shelf Russian Federation and in the Exclusive Economic Zone of Russian Federation in the performance of economic and (or) other activities, having a negative impact on the environment, with the exception of legal entities and individual entrepreneurs carrying out business and (or) other activities exclusively at the objects of category IV, wherein: (a) waste disposal, with the exception of solid municipal waste, the persons obliged to pay the fee are legal entities and individual entrepreneurs generating waste in the process of their business activities; (b) disposal of solid municipal waste by persons, obligated to pay a fee, are regional operators performing treatment of municipal solid waste, operators performing treatment of municipal solid waste and disposal thereof; (c) disposal of animal by-products recognized as waste; (d) disposal of industrial by-products recognized as waste; and (e) disposal of overburden and enclosing rocks recognized as waste. In case of waste disposal on sites excluding negative impact on the environment and determined in accordance with the legislation of the Russian Federation in the field of waste management, fees for negative impact from waste disposal will not be charged.

Policy: Regulation (EU) 2023/1115 on the making available on the Union market and the export from the Union of certain commodities and products associated with deforestation and forest degradation and repealing Regulation (EU) No 995/2010.
Policy_Content: This Regulation promotes the placing and making available on the Union market as well as the export from the Union of ‘deforestation-free’ products, with a view to: (a) minimizing the Union’s contribution to deforestation and forest degradation worldwide, and thereby contributing to a reduction in global deforestation; and (b) reducing the Union’s contribution to greenhouse gas emissions and global biodiversity loss. This Regulation sets out the obligations concerning relevant commodities and relevant products in order to effectively combat deforestation and forest degradation, and to promote deforestation-free supply chains, while taking into account the protection of human rights and the rights of indigenous peoples and local communities, both in the Union and in third countries. Article 3 allows the placing and making available on the Union market or exporting of relevant commodities and relevant products, only if they are (I) deforestation-free; (II) produced in accordance with the relevant legislation of the country of production; and (III) covered by a due diligence statement. Annex I lists relevant products that contain, have been fed with or have been made using relevant commodities, namely cattle, cocoa, coffee, oil palm, rubber, soya and wood, and Annex II sets out the information to be contained in the due diligence statement.

Policy: Executive Decree No. 78/23 approving the General Guidelines for the preparation of the Rural Electrification Plan.
Policy_Content: The main objective of the Rural Electrification Plan for Angola is to bring electricity to remote areas of the country that do not yet have access to the electricity grid and which are not expected to be connected to the national grid within 10 years. This objective involves electrifying these areas to improve the quality of life of the populations and promoting the economic and social development of these regions. This goal can be achieved through the installation of isolated systems (mini-grids) or solar kits, such as solar, wind and hydraulic energy, to supply electricity to these areas. The ultimate goal is the universal access to electricity by 2030 to promote economic and social development, improve people's quality of life and protect the environment, with an emphasis on the use of renewable, sustainable and economically viable energy technologies. The specific objectives of this Plan can be divided into short, medium and long term. The short-term objectives include establishing the political and regulatory framework for electrification through isolated systems and solar kits, as well as licensing and tendering processes. The short-term objectives include deepening planning and defining benefit systems to attract the private sector and validate business models.

Policy: The Carbon Accounting (Determination of Excess UK Assigned Amount Units) Regulations 2023 (S.I. 2023 No. 557).
Policy_Content: These Regulations make provision under section 27(5) of the Climate Change Act 2008 (c. 27) (“the Act”). Regulation 3 requires the Secretary of State to determine whether the UK’s emissions allowance under international emissions reduction targets are higher than the UK’s emissions allowance under domestic carbon budgets. Where the assigned amount is greater, regulation 3 requires the Secretary of State to calculate the number of UK assigned amount units representing the excess. Regulation 3 also sets out what the Secretary of State must take into account when calculating this and requires that UK assigned amount units in excess are not used to offset greenhouse gas emissions in the United Kingdom or elsewhere. These Regulations make provision under Section 27(5) of the Climate Change Act 2008 (“the Act”), which requires the Secretary of State to determine whether the UK’s emissions allowance under international emissions reduction targets are higher than the UK’s emissions allowance under domestic carbon budgets. Any excess units representing the difference in stringency between the domestic carbon budget and international targets are to be made unavailable to prevent the UK from using excess emissions allowances to offset greenhouse gas emissions in the UK or elsewhere. The relevant international agreement for these Regulations is the Doha Amendment to the Kyoto Protocol which makes provision for the Second Commitment Period (2013- 2020) (“the Second Commitment Period”). The corresponding period under domestic emission reduction targets made under the Act is Carbon Budget 2 (2013-2017) and the first three years of Carbon Budget 3 (2018-2020).

Policy: Ley Nº 21.562 - Modifica Ley Nº 19.300, sobre bases generales del medio ambiente, con el objeto de establecer restricciones a la evaluación de proyectos en zonas declaradas latentes o saturadas.
Policy_Content: La presente Ley introduce modificaciones a la Ley Nº 19.300 sobre bases generales del medio ambiente, con el objetivo de introducir restricciones a la evaluación de proyectos en zonas declaradas latentes o saturadas. Zonas latentes son aquellas en que la medición de la concentración de contaminantes en el aire, agua o suelo se sitúa entre el 80% y el 100% del valor de la respectiva norma de calidad ambiental. Zonas saturadas son aquellas en que una o más normas de calidad ambiental se encuentran sobrepasadas. Se incorporan las siguientes definiciones al artículo 2º: Impacto Crítico; Plan de Prevención; y Plan de Descontaminación. Se establece la obligación de elaborar un Estudio de Impacto Ambiental para aquellos proyectos o actividades que produzcan, como consecuencia de las emisiones estimadas del proyecto, un impacto significativo por la o las circunstancias que serán determinadas mediante el decreto que declare la zona saturada o latente, mientras no se dicten los respectivos planes de prevención o de descontaminación. Será rechazado aquel Estudio de Impacto Ambiental que, como consecuencia de las emisiones proyectadas del proyecto, produzca un impacto crítico en los componentes ambientales potencialmente afectados o en la salud de la población. Para estos efectos no será posible considerar la compensación de emisiones. Se agregan normas sobre el contenido del Decreto del artículo 43 que declara una zona del territorio como saturada o latente. Se incorpora un nuevo artículo 43 bis sobre la adopción de medidas provisionales de acuerdo a lo señalado en el artículo 32 de la ley N° 19.880, las que podrán mantenerse hasta la dictación del respectivo plan de prevención o descontaminación. Se agregan normas sobre los planes de prevención o de descontaminación del artículo 44 y sobre el desarrollo de actividades en aquellas áreas en que se esté aplicando un plan de prevención o descontaminación del artículo 46, referidas a la compensación de emisiones.

Policy: Presidential Decree No. PP-158 “On additional measures to further improve the system of ensuring seismic safety of the population and the national territory.
Policy_Content: The President, in order to introduce new methods for ensuring seismic safety, improve the seismic resistance of buildings and structures, put into practice a modern system for predicting strong earthquakes and preparing for them, decrees: (a) to gradually launch the National Early Warning System for Strong Earthquakes in the Republic from December 1, 2023 and determine the Ministry of Emergency Situations responsible for this system. This Presidential Decree establishes that within the framework of this National System, on the basis of integration with stations included in the global system of international seismic observations shall be performed the following actions: (a) monitoring of seismic phenomena in Uzbekistan and in the territories adjacent to it is carried out in real time; (b) after the registration of strong vibrations at two or more seismic stations located near the epicenter of the earthquake, and the determination of an earthquake in the national territory with a magnitude of 5 points and higher on the MSK-64 scale: by means of special programs at seismological stations, seismic data are automatically analyzed and earthquake parameters are promptly determined; through the mobile application "Strong Earthquake Alert" in a matter of seconds, an urgent notification is sent to the population about an impending strong earthquake in certain areas of the national territory. All costs associated with the launch of the National Early Warning System for Strong Earthquakes in the Republic of Uzbekistan are covered by the Fund for Support of the Sphere of Seismology, Seismic Resistance of Structures and Seismic Safety. Policy: Presidential Decree No. UP-144 “On measures to further improve the system of seismic safety”.
Policy_Content: The President, in order to ensure targeted reforms in the fields of seismology, ensuring the seismic resistance of structures and seismic safety, widespread introduction of digital technologies in the aforesaid fields, identifying priority areas for increasing training of highly qualified personnel to a qualitatively new level, decrees to approve the Concept for improving the system for ensuring seismic safety of the population and territory of the Republic of Uzbekistan until 2025 and “Road map” for the implementation in 2022-2023 of the Concept. The Concept defines strategic goals, priority areas, tasks, plans for the medium and long-term development of the field of seismology, ensuring the seismic resistance of structures and seismic safety in the Republic of Uzbekistan, and is also the basis for the development of programs and comprehensive measures in the aforesaid field. State policy in the field of seismology, ensuring the seismic resistance of structures and seismic safety is aimed at ensuring the successful implementation of programs across the country, regions and industries, increasing the potential of the field through the effective use of scientific and technical resources. The strategic objectives of ensuring seismic safety of the population and territory of the Republic of Uzbekistan are: (a) training all segments of the population for the activities during and after an earthquake and developing comprehensive measures to improve their preparedness; (b) development of scientific, practical and innovative research on the implementation of seismic hazard, impact and risk assessment based on foreign experience and the development of regulatory legal acts on their basis; (c) assessment of various levels of seismic risk in seismically active zones and development of scientifically based measures to reduce losses from earthquakes; (d) implementation of the development of a draft master plan for urban areas based on seismic microzoning maps; (e) expansion of fundamental, applied, innovative and investment projects in the field of seismic resistance of buildings, structures and communications, structural strength, development and widespread implementation in practice of recommendations and proposals for improving seismic construction technologies; (f) scientific developments in the field of seismic resistance and ensuring seismic safety of structures, ensuring their implementation in the field of seismic safety; (g) development of a set of measures for areas with a high probability of earthquakes to reduce the consequences of their damage, taking into account local conditions; (h) creation of a system for monitoring the seismic resistance of reservoir dams and hydraulic structures; (i) creation of an acceptable legal, investment and infrastructure environment to support and accelerate the development of research to ensure seismic safety of the national territory; and (j) training of qualified personnel in the field of seismic safety, advanced training of scientists in leading foreign scientific centers and manufacturing enterprises, development of international cooperation.

Policy: Regulation No. 686 of the Cabinet of Ministers on sustainability and greenhouse gas emissions savings criteria, criteria for electricity produced from biomass fuel and procedures for justifying, certifying and monitoring compliance with said criteria.
Policy_Content: This Regulation establishes essential requirements for a specific type of fuel, as well as for electricity produced from forest biomass with a view of ensuring sustainability and greenhouse gas emission saving criteria and specific criteria for electricity, as well as a mechanism for monitoring and checking their implementation and compliance with the requirements; and appoints institutions that carry out compliance certification in the regulated sphere, sets forth voluntary schemes and their monitoring procedures, as well as institutions that carry out compliance certification and supervision of the object of conformity assessment. Biomass fuel must meet  the sustainability and greenhouse gas emission savings criteria if: (a) it is used in an installation for the production of electricity, heat, energy for cooling or refrigeration, or for the production of fuels, the total nominal input heat output of which, summing up the output of all stationary technological combustion equipment, is 20 megawatts (MW) or more in the case of solid biomass fuel, or 2 megawatts (MW ) or greater in the case of gaseous biomass fuel; and (b) it is used in a facility for the production of electricity, thermal energy, energy required for cooling or freezing, or in a fuel production facility where, in accordance with the regulations on pollution, the polluting activities included in the European Union emission allowance trading system are carried out and which requires a greenhouse gas emission permit. Biofuel, bioliquid fuel, biomass fuel and biomass fuel produced from agricultural biomass must not be produced from raw materials obtained from high biodiversity value land areas, that is, land that was granted on or after January 2008 one of the following statuses (whether or not the land still has this status): (a) primeval forests and other forest lands; (b) biodiverse forest and other wooded land that is rich in species and not degraded or recognized as land of high biological diversity; (c) protected areas; (d) micro-reserves created for the protection of protected species and protected habitats and territories that protect rare, threatened or endangered ecosystems; and (e) grasslands and meadows with high biological diversity.

Policy: Real Decreto 366/2023 - Por el que se establecen las bases reguladoras para la concesión de subvenciones a la cooperación para la preparación y ejecución de proyectos de innovación de interés general llevados a cabo por grupos operativos supraautonómicos de la Asociación Europea para la Innovación en materia de productividad y sostenibilidad agrícolas (AEI-Agri).
Policy_Content: El presente Real Decreto tiene por objeto establecer las bases reguladoras para la concesión de subvenciones  destinadas a la cooperación para la preparación y ejecución de proyectos de innovación de interés general para el desarrollo de nuevos productos, prácticas, procesos o servicios, desarrollos experimentales o innovación en materia de organización o de procesos de transformación y comercialización, en los sectores agrícola, ganadero, forestal y agroalimentario. Los proyectos serán llevados a cabo por grupos operativos supraautonómicos de la Asociación Europea para la Innovación en materia de productividad y sostenibilidad agrícolas (AEIAgri), definidos en el artículo 3. Los proyectos a financiar deben estar orientados a beneficiar a todo un sector o subsector en el ámbito nacional y se ejecutarán en el territorio de al menos dos comunidades autónomas. Se establecen los requisitos que deberán cumplir los beneficiarios. Podrán ser beneficiarias de las subvenciones las agrupaciones que se asocien para formar parte de un grupo operativo supraautonómico de la AEI-Agri, para preparar y ejecutar un proyecto innovador conforme al artículo 1. Las integrantes del grupo operativo podrán ser: a) Del sector agroalimentario y forestal; b) Del sector investigador o del conocimiento; y b) organizaciones no gubernamentales o similares. El límite máximo de estas ayudas se determinará en la correspondiente convocatoria y en ningún caso superará los 600.000 euros por agrupación beneficiaria y proyecto, para los proyectos en los que la innovación se oriente a los productos del anexo I del Tratado de Funcionamiento de la Unión Europea, o de 500.000 euros en los casos restantes.

Policy_Content: This Regulation determines the amount of the state fee and the payment procedure for the license to use the subsoil, the frequently encountered mineral extraction permit, the mineral deposit certificate and the coordination of the blasting work project to be carried out at the mineral extraction sites. The state fee for the subsoil use license, common mineral extraction permit and mineral deposit passport shall be paid before submitting the application for the relevant subsoil use license, common mineral extraction permit or mineral deposit passport for obtaining a deposit passport. The state fee for approval of the project of blasting works to be carried out at the mineral extraction site is paid before the project is submitted for approval. Payment is made using a non-cash payment in one of the following ways: (a) through a payment institution that has the right to provide payment services within the meaning of the Law on Payment Services and Electronic Money. When submitting an application to the State Environmental Service, indicate information about the fee payment made; and (b) using the online payment service in the information system of the State Environmental Service. The state fee for the subsoil use license, mineral deposit passport and approval of the project of blasting shall be included in the state basic budget, but the state fee for the frequently occurring mineral extraction permit - in the budget of the local municipality, whose administrative the territory contains common minerals.

Policy: Arrêté du 13 mai 2023 relatif aux définitions transversales relatives à l’activité et aux surfaces agricoles, à partir de la campagne 2023, dans le cadre de la politique agricole commune (rectificatif)
Policy_Content: Pour l’application de l’article D. 614-4 du code rural et de la pêche maritime, les critères à remplir par les agriculteurs pour respecter l’obligation de maintien d’une surface dans un état qui la rend adaptée au pâturage ou à la culture, sans action préparatoire allant au-delà du recours à des pratiques agricoles courantes et à des machines agricoles courantes, sont les suivants: 1) Sur terres arables: l’activité d’entretien est vérifiée par la détection ou la preuve d’une intervention sur la parcelle en complément de l’activité végétale ou, à défaut, pour les surfaces en jachère ou en herbe, par une absence d’enfrichement; 2) Sur cultures permanentes: l’entretien est vérifié par le maintien de la culture dans un état apte à la production qui est attesté:  – pour les cultures permanentes constituées d’espèces ligneuses (arbres, arbustes ou vignes), par le remplacement des arbres, arbustes ou pieds de vignes morts, par l’entretien des arbres, arbustes et pieds de vignes et par l’absence d’enfrichement de la parcelle; – pour les autres cultures permanentes, par la détection ou la preuve d’une intervention sur la parcelle en complément de l’activité végétale. Les cultures permanentes pour lesquelles l’entretien peut être effectué tous les deux ans sont les vergers; 3) Sur prairies permanentes: a) Sur les prairies permanentes majoritairement en herbe, l’activité d’entretien est vérifiée par l’absence d’enfrichement; b) Sur les surfaces couvertes par des espèces végétales ligneuses adaptées au pâturage et accessibles aux animaux, sans prédominance ou en l’absence d’herbe et d’autres plantes fourragères herbacées (à l’exception des chênaies et châtaigneraies), qui peuvent être admissibles dans les 38 départements définis à l’annexe 3 en application de l’article D. 614-8 du code rural et de la pêche maritime, l’activité d’entretien est vérifiée par le respect des critères cumulatifs suivants: « – le respect d’un taux de chargement minimal ou, à défaut, l’entretien par fauche ou broyage de l’intégralité des parcelles concernées; – et l’absence d’enfrichement.

Policy: Presidential Decree No. PK-156 “On measures to introduce the system of "Green Energy" certificates”.
Policy_Content: The President, in order to develop the use of renewable energy sources, decrees to introduce the system of "green energy" certificates of the Ministry of Economy and Finance, the Ministry of Energy and the joint-stock company "Uzbekgidroenergo" confirming that electricity is produced using renewable sources: (a) from July 1, 2023 - for electricity produced at hydroelectric power stations in the system of joint-stock company "Uzbekgidroenergo"; and (b) from October 1, 2023 - to approve the introduction of electricity produced using solar, wind and hydroelectric power stations and other renewable energy sources. Establish such a procedure, according to which: (a) one "green energy" certificate confirms the production of 1000 kWh of electricity using renewable energy sources; (b) the Ministry of Economy and Finance (issuer) is the body responsible for maintaining the system of "green energy" certificates, in particular, registering generation facilities, issuing "green energy" certificates, issuing them to generation facilities, and keeping track of their activity; (c) "green energy" certificates can be freely circulated and can be transferred from one person to another according to the procedure or method established by law; (d) "green energy" certificates can be transferred to other persons when electricity is sold or in cases not related to such sale; and (e) registration of generating facilities, issuance of "green energy" certificates with a unique identification number, accounting for their movement is carried out through the unified electronic platform of "Green Energy" certificates based on the requirements of international standards. Starting from July 1, 2023, legal entities and individuals shall be given the right to cover the energy share that is lacking in meeting the requirements for increasing the share of energy produced using renewable energy sources in the amount of energy consumption, determined by the competent authorities, at the expense of the appropriate number of "green energy" certificates.  Income from the sale of "green energy" certificates of generation facilities based on the use of renewable sources should be exempted from profit tax.

Policy: Law No. LP98/2022 “On atmospheric air quality”.
Policy_Content: The scope of this Law is to create a legal framework to strengthen institutional capacity for monitoring and assessing air quality to identify and apply effective emission reduction measures of air pollutants to levels that minimize overall harmful effects on human health and the environment. This Law regulates measures at national level regarding: (a) monitoring and assessing air quality throughout the national territory based on common methods and criteria established in accordance with the requirements of European Union standards and international treaties, to which the Republic of Moldova is a party; (b) obtaining information on ambient air quality to facilitate combating air pollution and the negative consequences it causes, and also for long-term monitoring of trends and improvements as a result of adopted national and regional measures; (c) providing the public with information about the quality of atmospheric air; (d) maintaining air quality where it meets air quality standards established in Annex 2, and its improvement in other cases; (e) ensuring cooperation with neighboring States to reduce air pollution; and (f) ensuring the fulfillment of obligations undertaken within the framework of international agreements to which the Republic of Moldova is a party. This Law establishes standards, assessment regimes and regimes of air quality management, territorial division criteria of the Republic of Moldova into zones and agglomerations, as well as protection measures to maintain air quality in accordance with European Union standards. When implementing this Law, the following principles are observed: (a) the principle of sustainable air quality management; (b) the principle of preventing air pollution; (c) the principle of prudence in decision making; (d) the “polluter pays” principle; and (e) the principle of transparency and accessibility of information and data. Ambient air quality is assessed based on limit values observed during a certain period of time, which cannot be exceeded once they are reached. The National Air Pollutant Emission Inventory System ensures the collection of the necessary data, as well as the processing of information in order to develop a national inventory of air pollutant emissions. The Environment Agency annually provides the public with quality report through any readily available media on atmospheric air quality at the national level for all pollutants. This Law contains IX Chapters divided into 45 Articles. Chapter I lays down general provisions. Chapter II establishes powers and duties. Chapter III regards quality assessment of atmospheric air. Chapter IV regards monitoring and management of air quality. Chapter V regards measures for the protection of atmospheric air. Chapter VI regards information and accountability. Chapter VII regards international cooperation. Chapter VIII establishes powers to exercise control and liability for violation of the legislation on atmospheric air quality. Chapter IX lays down final and transitional provisions.

Policy_Content: El presente real decreto-ley tiene por objeto establecer medidas de apoyo a los titulares de explotaciones agrarias que han visto agravada su situación por el contexto climatológico de sequía y elevadas temperaturas, que se ha sumado a la grave situación generada por la guerra de Ucrania, para de esa forma contribuir a garantizar la seguridad alimentaria y a la corrección de los desequilibrios del mercado. Con estas medidas se apoya a los agricultores y ganaderos que llevan a cabo su actividad ajustándose a los principios de economía circular, gestión de nutrientes, uso eficiente de los recursos y utilizando métodos de producción respetuosos con el medio ambiente y el clima, incluidos en la normativa europea y nacional. Además, el real decreto-ley tiene por objeto paliar los graves e imprevisibles daños derivados de la sequía mediante el establecimiento de medidas de gestión y de apoyo para los abastecimientos y regadíos situados en los ámbitos territoriales afectados por la sequía en el año 2023, así como la identificación de determinadas actuaciones de ejecución inmediata y prioritarias necesarias para afrontar con inmediatez los problemas derivados de la sequía. Del mismo modo, se incorporan determinadas medidas en materia de transportes y de seguridad laboral.

Policy: Regulation (EU) 2023/956 establishing a carbon border adjustment mechanism.
Policy_Content: This Regulation establishes a carbon border adjustment mechanism (CBAM) to address greenhouse gas emissions embedded in the goods listed in Annex I on their importation into the customs territory of the Union in order to prevent the risk of carbon leakage, thereby reducing global carbon emissions and supporting the goals of the Paris Agreement, also by creating incentives for the reduction of emissions by operators in third countries. The CBAM complements the system for greenhouse gas emission allowance trading within the Union established under Directive 2003/87/EC by applying an equivalent set of rules to imports into the customs territory of the Union of the goods referred to in Article 2 of this Regulation. The CBAM replaces the mechanisms established under Directive 2003/87/EC to prevent the risk of carbon leakage by reflecting the extent to which EU Emissions Trading System allowances are allocated free of charge in accordance with Article 10a of that Directive.

Policy_Content: This Order establishes classification of natural and man-made emergency situations. Policy: Regulation 2023/955 establishing a Social Climate Fund and amending Regulation (EU) 2021/1060.
Policy_Content: This Regulation establishes the Social Climate Fund for the period from 2026 to 2032. The Fund shall provide financial support to Member States for the measures and investments included in their Social Climate Plans. The measures and investments supported by the Fund shall benefit households, micro-enterprises and transport users, which are vulnerable and particularly affected by the inclusion of greenhouse gas emissions from buildings and road transport within the scope of Directive 2003/87/EC, in particular households in energy poverty or households in transport poverty. Policy_Content: This Code regulates national maritime spaces, as well as situations and legal relationships arising from maritime navigation. Without prejudice to the provisions of each of its Books, and to international law rules binding the State of Cape Verde, the provisions of this Code apply to any ship, whatever its nationality or the nationality and residence of its owners or shipowners. Policy: Arrêté du Gouvernement flamand réglant la consultation transfrontalière en cas d’évaluation des incidences sur l’environnement de projets d’autres pays ou régions, visée à l’article 4.3.9, § 5, du décret du 5 avril 1995 contenant des dispositions générales concernant la politique de l’environnement.
Policy_Content: Le présent arrêté est fondé sur : - la loi spéciale du 8 août 1980 de réformes institutionnelles, article 20 ; - le décret du 5 avril 1995 contenant des dispositions générales concernant la politique de l’environnement, article 4.3.9, § 5, inséré par le décret du 18 décembre 2015. Le présent arrêté est proposé par la ministre flamande de la Justice et du Maintien, de l’Environnement et de l’Aménagement du Territoire, de l’Énergie et du Tourisme. Le présent arrêté prévoit la transposition partielle de la directive 2011/92/UE du Parlement européen et du Conseil du 13 décembre 2011 concernant l’évaluation des incidences de certains projets publics et privés sur l’environnement. Lorsque le département reçoit une notification d’une autorité compétente concernant une demande d’autorisation comprenant un RIE du projet susceptible d’avoir des incidences sur l’environnement transfrontalières ou transrégionales, il examine s’il souhaite participer au processus décisionnel en matière d’environnement concernant le projet prévu, et, le cas échéant, il informe l’autorité compétente concernée de sa décision. Lorsqu’une administration compétente reçoit une notification des autorités compétentes concernant une demande d’autorisation comprenant un RIE du projet susceptible d’avoir des incidences sur l’environnement transfrontalières ou transrégionales sur son territoire, elle en informe le département. Si le département constate que, sur la base des informations fournies par la notification, il n’est pas en mesure de décider de participer ou non au processus décisionnel en matière d’environnement, il demande à l’autorité compétente les informations manquantes de la notification.

Policy: Ley Nº 8 – Que establece la conservación y protección de las tortugas marinas y sus hábitats en la República de Panamá.
Policy_Content: La presente Ley tiene por objeto proteger y conservar todas las especies de tortugas marinas presentes en el territorio nacional de Panamá, así como garantizar la restauración, prevención de contaminación y degradación de los habitats de las tortugas marinas, y establecer acciones y medidas necesarias para asegurar la resiliencia y supervivencia de estas especies. Se declara de interés publico la protección, conservación y manejo de las tortugas marinas y sus habitats. El Ministerio de Ambiente deberá establecer áreas protegidas, zonas especiales de manejo y zonas de reserva y decretar cualquier otra medida de conservación y/o rehabilitación que se requiera para la protección de las tortugas marinas, sus huevos, neonatos y habitats. La Ley crea el Comité Nacional para la Protección, Conservación y Manejo Sostenible de las Tortugas Marinas, estableciendo sus integrantes y funciones. Se regula asimismo las actividades de turismo y su impacto en las tortugas marinas. El Artículo 29 de la Ley otorga derechos legales a las tortugas marinas, tales como vivir y tener paso libre en un ambiente sano, libre de contaminación y otros impactos antropocéntricos que causan daño físico y a la salud, permitiendo que las personas naturales y jurídicas protejan dichos derechos. Quedan prohibidos la captura, asedio o maltrato, cautiverio, pesca intencional, retención, procesamiento o muerte intencional de las tortugas marinas en todo el territorio nacional.

Policy: Water Resources (Control of Agricultural Pollution) (Wales) Regulations 2021 No. 77 (W. 20).
Policy_Content: These Regulations are organised in 8 Parts. Part 1 contains introductory provisions including transitional provision for all holdings not previously within a Nitrate Vulnerable Zone. Part 2 imposes annual limits on the amount of nitrogen from organic manure that may be applied or spread. Part 3 sets requirements and limits relating to the amount of nitrogen to be spread on a crop; it also establishes that an occupier must plan in advance the spreading of nitrogen fertiliser, record additional information during the year. Part 4 regulates the spreading of nitrogen fertilizer, where and when to spread it, conditions when the spreading happens near surface water, control system among others. Part 5 establishes closed periods during which it is prohibited to spread nitrogen fertilizer. Part 6 makes provision for the storage of organic manure and prescribes the capacity and construction requirements for such storage systems. Part 7 specifies what records must be kept. Part 9 contains criminal offences and enforcement provisions.

Policy: Decree No. 171 of the Cabinet of Ministers “On measures to effectively organize the activities of the state system to prevent emergency situations and act in such situations in the Republic of Uzbekistan”.
Policy_Content: Regulation on the State System of Prevention of Emergency Situations and Action in Such Situations of the Republic of Uzbekistan, contained in Annex 1, stipulates the composition, main objectives and tasks, organizational and functional structure and the procedure of operation of the State System of Prevention of Emergency Situations and Action in Such Situations of the Republic of Uzbekistan. The functions of the national executive authorities of and other organizations for the protection of the population and territories against emergency situations within the framework of the functional sub-system of the state system of prevention of emergency situations and action in such situations of the Republic of Uzbekistan are contained in the Annex 2. The functions of the local executive authorities to protect the population and territories against emergency situations within the framework of the territorial sub-system of the state system of emergency prevention and action in such situations of the Republic of Uzbekistan are contained in the Annex 3. Natural and man-made emergency situations shall be considered an accident, destruction, dangerous event that may lead to the death of people in a certain area, damage to people's health or the natural environment, serious material losses, and disruption of people's living conditions, situations arising as a result of a natural event, natural phenomena or other disaster, as a result of the spread of quarantine and other infectious diseases dangerous to humans. The main goal of the State system for prevention of emergency situations and action in such situations is to ensure the effective organization and implementation of measures to prevent and eliminate emergency situations in peace and special times by republican and local executive authorities and other organizations that have powers in the field of protection against emergency situations or are assigned obligations in this field. The information-management structure of the State system for prevention of emergency situations and action in such situations includes the following: National Center for Action and Management in Emergency Situations; information centers of the monitoring and control bodies of the natural environment and high-risk objects; stationary (fixed) control points; points of action for managing emergency response forces and means; duty-dispatching services of regional and functional sub-systems; means of communication and information transfer, including the automated system of management and information provision.

Policy: Decree No. 169 of the Cabinet of Ministers “On measures to recultivate degraded lands, preserve the fertile layer of the soil and organize its rational use”.
Policy_Content: The Regulation on the procedure for the recultivation of disturbed lands, extraction, preservation and rational use of the fertile layer of the soil, envisages the application of the following arrangements: (a) the procedure for establishing a commission for recultivation of disturbed lands, determination of disturbed lands and acceptance of recultivated lands, as well as its rights and obligations; (b) procedure for extracting and preserving the fertile layer of land by individuals and legal entities carrying out industrial, construction, and other activities related to the destruction of the soil layer; (c) procedure for accepting and handing over recultivated land after receiving a written notification from natural persons and legal entities about the completion of recultivation works; (d) the procedure for developing a project for the recultivation of disturbed land and carrying out the recultivation at the expense of the natural person or legal entity that caused the disturbance of the land. The Ministry of Natural Resources of the Republic of Uzbekistan, the Ministry of Agriculture and the Ministry of Mining and Geology, the Mining, Geological and Industrial Safety Control Inspectorate within its powers recultivate disturbed lands and restore their productivity, extract and preserve the fertile layer of the soil and ensure effective control and monitoring of the quality and timeliness of its use. Starting from May 1, 2023: (a) the users of the agricultural land allocated for the expansion of the city of Tashkent and cities in other regions and for non-agricultural purposes will extract the fertile layer of the soil from these land plots and ensure that they are delivered to the land areas where they will be used, and recultivation works will be carried out; (b) during the period of recultivation of degraded lands intended for agriculture, development of projects for the designation of protected areas of infrastructure objects, and during the period of relocation of the project, authorship control shall be carried out by the State Scientific-Design Institute of the Ministry of Agriculture of the Republic of Uzbekistan "Uzdaverloyiha" and its regional divisions; and (c) recultivation activities and design works of agricultural lands damaged due to overturning of mining resources, as well as due to the construction of infrastructure objects (roads, pipelines, electric networks) are carried out at the expense of natural persons and legal entities who built these infrastructure objects. The Ministry of Agriculture of the Republic of Uzbekistan, together with the relevant ministries and agencies, shall ensure that prior to August 1, 2023, the database on the state of agricultural land contained in all categories of the land fund, including disturbed and recultivated land, shall be kept in the "Geoinformation" system of the Ministry of Agriculture.

Control of agricultural, reclamation and road construction equipment, repair and service equipment is carried out by the Inspectorate. Upon the expiration of the equipment leasing (sublease) agreement, the equipment is transferred to the state register in the name of the lessee based on the equipment leasing (sublease) agreement and the transfer-acceptance document confirming that the equipment lessor's property rights to the equipment have been transferred to the equipment lessee. Agricultural, land reclamation and road construction machinery, as well as service and repair equipment and other equipment of physical and legal entities shall be subject to mandatory annual technical inspection. Annex 1 contains technical passport issued to agriculture, land reclamation and road construction equipment and self-driving cars. Annex 2 contains the form of technical certificate of equipment. Policy: Decree No. 11.509 creating the National Council for Indigenous Policy.
Policy_Content: This Decree creates the National Council for Indigenous Policy (CNPI) under the Ministry of Indigenous Peoples, a consultative collegiate, responsible for preparing and monitoring the implementation of public policies aimed at indigenous peoples. The CNPI is responsible to: propose objectives and principles for public policies aimed at indigenous peoples; monitor the implementation of public policies aimed at indigenous peoples; support the integration and articulation of governmental and non-governmental bodies that make up the CNPI and work with indigenous peoples or whose actions affect them; encourage harmonization between specific, differentiated public policies directed at indigenous peoples; propose the holding of National Conferences on Indigenous Policy; support the promotion, in conjunction with government agencies and indigenous-related entities, of educational campaigns on the rights of indigenous peoples and respect for their ethnic and cultural diversity; propose technical training actions to qualify the performance of government agents and representatives of indigenous peoples in indigenous-related policy; support and encourage the holding of events organized by indigenous peoples, especially for the debate and improvement of public policy proposals for them; monitor the preparation and execution of the Union's General Budget, within the scope of public policies aimed at indigenous peoples; contribute to the creation of an information system that integrates, in a single easily accessible platform, the various existing databases on population, health, education, territoriality and other relevant issues of indigenous peoples in the country; monitor and, eventually, receive and forward reports of threats or violations of the rights of the indigenous community or people to the competent bodies, in addition to recommending the measures to be adopted; draw up its bylaws; and monitor proposals for normative acts and administrative and judicial decisions that may affect the rights of indigenous peoples.

Policy: Law No. 21.894 on the prohibition of the application of pesticides containing the active ingredient named fipronil in the specified areas.
Policy_Content: This Law establishes the prohibition of the sprayed application of pesticides containing the active ingredient fipronil within specified areas. Policy: Resolution No. 15/2023 creating the Technical-Scientific Commission on Climate Change (CTCMC).
Policy_Content: This Resolution creates the Technical-Scientific Commission on Climate Change (CTCMC), a consultation and technical advisory body, aimed to support the prevention, adaptation and mitigation of Climate Change. CTCMC is responsible for: a) advising the Government on mitigation management measures relating to the environmental and social effects of extreme weather events, as well as human action with a negative impact on the environment; b) drawing up the current situation and risks and defining a programme of focused thematic and territorial actions; c) identifying priority intervention areas; d) evaluating the efficiency of the intervening institutions in the prevention, mitigation and monitoring of the negative impacts of climatic phenomena and human action on the environment; e) assessing policies, strategies and other instruments aimed to respond to the impacts of climate change and human action; f) advising on technical and scientific solutions to increase the efficiency of prevention and response to extreme events, with a view to creating greater human, infrastructure and ecosystem resilience; g) monitoring progress in implementing action plans to adapt and mitigate the effects of climate change; h) analysing potential risk scenarios of extreme events; i) advising on actions to improve and strengthen inter-institutional coordination with all entities in preventing and responding to the impact of the effects of climate change and climate change and harmful action of man on the environment, etc.

Policy: Sea Pollution (Ballast Water Management Convention) Regulations 2023 (S.I. No. 188/2023).
Policy_Content: These Regulations apply to (a) Irish ships; (b) ships, although not entitled to fly the flag of the State, operate under the authority of the State, and (c) ships, other than those referred to in paragraphs (a) and (b), that enter a port, harbor or repair yard in the State. The owner of a ship (in these Regulations referred to as “ship owner”) is responsible for ensuring compliance with the requirements set out in these Regulations. The Regulations establish design and construction requirements of ballast water management systems. The ballast water management system shall also have a suitable control and monitoring system that will automatically monitor and record sufficient data to verify the correct operation of the system. Type approval process and certification is regulated by Regulation 7. Each ship ship shall have on board a Ballast Water Management Plan along with a designated officer charged with ensuring that the plan is properly implemented and a Ballast Water Record Book  In the case of an Irish ship, the plan shall be approved by the MSO, taking into account Guidelines. The Ballast Water Management Plan shall contain the following: safety procedures, as set out in Guidelines, for the ship and the crew associated with ballast water management; detailed description of the actions to be taken to implement the plan, including the ballast water management requirements; procedures for the disposal of sediments at sea and to shore;  procedures for coordinating with authorities of a state in a situation where ballast water management involves discharge into the territorial seas of that state; details of the designated officer and other requirement.

Policy: Law No. 122-VII ZRK “On biological safety”.
Policy_Content: This Law defines the legal basis for state regulation in the field of biological safety of the Republic of Kazakhstan and is aimed at prevention of biological threats. This Law regulates public relations concerning the treatment of pathogenic biological agents, in order to ensure biological safety. Biological safety shall be intended the state of protection of people, individuals and components of the natural environment (atmospheric air, surface and underground waters, earth's surface and soil layer, flora and fauna and other organisms from hazardous biological factors, including those provided by biological protection measures. Biological risk shall be intended the likelihood of causing harm to the health of people and animals, plants with pathogenic biological agents, as well as the likelihood of their entry into individual components of the natural environment. Handling of pathogenic biological agents shall be intended processes (stages) of work with pathogenic biological agents directly aimed at allocation (discovery), development (creation), production (manufacturing), turnover (including import (export), storage, transportation) of pathogenic biological agents for the purpose of their research, destruction and (or) development of immunobiological preparations. Biological safety is ensured in line with the following principles: (a) handling of pathogenic biological agents exclusively in non-military purposes: it is prohibited handling of pathogenic biological agents for the purposes of development (creation), production (manufacturing) and (or) stockpiling, use of bacteriological (biological) and toxin weapons; (b) early recognition of biological threats: state authorities, when exercising powers in the field of biological safety, must be guided by the need for prevention as a priority biological threats, analyze and predict biological threats based on accounting and monitoring data in the field of biological safety; (c) controllability of handling pathogenic biological agents: pathogenic biological agents are handled in accordance with requirements in the field of biological safety, compliance with which is provided within the framework of biological risk management, application of authorization procedure for handling pathogenic biological agents, accounting, monitoring and forecasting (modeling) in the field of biological safety, government control and supervision of compliance with requirements in areas of biological safety; (d)  proportionality of government regulation measures: preventive measures in biosafety areas must be proportionate to the degree of hazardousness of biological factors, including in accordance with the criteria and classification in areas of biological safety; and (e) priority of national interests of the Republic of Kazakhstan: it is not allowed acceptance of obligations within the framework of international cooperation that do not correspond to the national interests of the Republic of Kazakhstan that could cause damage to the national security of the Republic of Kazakhstan or leading to loss of independence of the Republic of Kazakhstan. Main problems and threats, strategic goals, main directions, target indicators, objectives and outcome indicators, interdepartmental interaction in the field of biological safety is determined by the Strategy of national security of the Republic of Kazakhstan. State regulation in the field of biological safety is carried out by: (a) implementation of a unified state policy in the field of biological safety; (b) introduction of authorization procedure for handling pathogenic biological agents; (c) carrying out state control and supervision over compliance with requirements in the field of biological safety; (d) biological risk management; and (e) accounting, monitoring and forecasting (modeling) in the field of biological safety. Handling of pathogenic biological agents is based on the classification of pathogenic biological agents according to pathogenicity and degree of hazardousness: (a) pathogenicity group I - pathogenic biological agents that cause particularly dangerous infectious diseases of people and (or) animals with a high level of mortality (lethality), easily spread from an infected person the body to a healthy one, as a rule, for which there are no vaccines or effective therapies; (b) pathogenicity group II - pathogenic biological agents that cause infectious and (or) parasitic diseases in humans and (or) animals, easily spreading from an infected organism to a healthy one, for which effective means and methods of treatment and prevention are available, including vaccines. This group is divided into pathogenic biological agents that cause: particularly dangerous infectious diseases; infectious and (or) parasitic diseases; (c) III group of pathogenicity - pathogenic biological agents that cause infectious and (or) parasitic diseases of humans and (or) animals or can cause significant harm to plants, characterized by minimal spread from an infected organism to a healthy one, for which effective means and methods of treatment are available and prevention, including vaccines; and (d) IV group of pathogenicity - pathogenic biological agents that cause infectious and (or) parasitic diseases of people and (or) animals or can cause harm to plants, as a rule, do not spread from an infected organism to a healthy one, for which effective means and methods of treatment are available and prevention, including vaccines. This Law contains 8 Chapters divided into 32 Articles. Chapter 1 lays down basic provisions. Chapter 2 regards state regulation in the field of biosafety. Chapter 3 establishes general requirements for ensuring biosafety. Chapter 4 establishes state control and supervision over compliance with the requirements in the field of biosafety. Chapter 5 regards collections of microorganisms. Chapter 6 regards social protection of experts and auxiliary staff. Chapter 7 regards scientific and educational activity in the field of biosafety. Chapter 8 lays down final and transitional provisions.

Policy: Regulation (EU) 2023/857 amending Regulation (EU) 2018/842 on binding annual greenhouse gas emission reductions by Member States from 2021 to 2030 contributing to climate action to meet commitments under the Paris Agreement, and Regulation (EU) 2018/1999.
Policy_Content: This Regulation amends the subject matter of Regulation (EU) 2018/842 as "This Regulation lays down obligations on Member States with respect to their minimum contributions for the period from 2021 to 2030 to fulfilling the Union’s target of reducing its greenhouse gas emissions by 40 % below 2005 levels in 2030 in the sectors covered by Article 2 of this Regulation. It contributes to the long-term target of climate neutrality in the Union at the latest by 2050, with the aim of achieving negative emissions thereafter. It thereby contributes to achieving the objectives of Regulation (EU) 2021/1119 and the Paris Agreement. This Regulation also lays down rules on determining annual emission allocations and for the evaluation of Member States’ progress towards meeting their minimum contributions". This Regulation makes amendments in Article 2 regarding the sectors covered by the Regulation (EU) 2018/842; Article 4 regarding the limitation of greenhouse gas emissions by each Member State in accordance with Annex I; Article 5 regarding flexibilities by means of borrowing, banking and transfer by the Member States from their annual emission allocation, in respect of the years 2021 to 2025; Article 6 regarding flexibility for certain Member States following reduction of EU ETS allowances; Article 7 regarding additional use of net removals from land use, land-use change and forestry (LULUCF); Article 8 regarding corrective actions; Article 15 regarding review of Regulation (EU) 2018/842 taking into account, inter alia, evolving national circumstances, the manner in which all sectors of the economy contribute to the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions, international developments and efforts undertaken to achieve the long-term objectives of the Paris Agreement and of Regulation (EU) 2021/1119. This Regulation amends Annexes I, II and III to Regulation (EU) 2018/842 and inserts Article 15a on scientific advice on Union measures, climate targets, annual emission levels and flexibilities under this Regulation. Furthermore, this Regulation amends Article 26 of the Regulation 2018/1999 regarding the obligation of Member States to report on the final greenhouse gas inventory data, and point (n) of Annex V regarding the information to be included in the report.

Policy: Law No. 22/X/2023 establishing the Legal Regime for the commercialization, importation, distribution and production of single-use plastic.
Policy_Content: This Law, consisting of 27 articles and one Annex, establishes the Legal Regime for the Marketing, Import, Distribution and Production of Single-Use Plastic materials and objects produced with plastic materials. This Law applies to all sectors of economic and industrial activity and to all economic agents engaged in both wholesale and retail trade, formal or informal, and to all stages of manufacture, processing and distribution of materials and single-use plastic objects, with the exception of the areas of health, cosmetics and personal hygiene. Plastic materials and articles are manufactured in accordance with good manufacturing practices, so that, under foreseeable conditions of use, they do not transfer their constituents into the contents in quantities that could: a) represent a danger to human health; b) cause an unacceptable change in the composition of the food; or c) cause a deterioration of its organoleptic characteristics. Prohibition of placing single-use plastic objects on the market and inspection to detect non-compliance with measures and standards are detailed in the Law.

Policy_Content: This Act comprising 30 Sections aims at promoting and enhancing rural electrification which continues to be conducted by the Rural Electrification Authority established under the repealed Act. The Rural Electrification Fund, established under the repealed Act, continues, with the main purpose of increasing and sustaining the availability of electricity in rural areas and ensuring access to electricity to the rural population. Policy_Content: This Regulation determines the procedure for granting, administering and monitoring public and European Union support for beekeeping in the planning period 2023-2027, calculated on annual basis. The Rural Support Service allocates, administers and monitors the use of support funding, as well as performs inspections in accordance with the regulatory enactments on the procedure for administering and monitoring the European Agricultural Guarantee Fund and the European Agricultural Fund for Rural Development, as well as public and the European Union support for agriculture and rural development for the period of 2023-2027. Support funding is granted annually in the period from October 16 of the current year to October 15 of the following year for the following types of interventions and the achievement of the goals set in them: (a) advisory services, technical assistance, training, exchange of information and best practices, including through networking, for beekeepers and beekeepers' organizations; (b) investments in tangible and intangible assets and other measures aimed also at combating bee parasites and diseases, especially varrosa; (c) investments in tangible and intangible assets and other measures also aimed at preventing damage caused by adverse climatic conditions and promoting the development and use of management practices suitable for changing climatic conditions; (d) investments in tangible and intangible assets and other measures also aimed at updating the number of bees in hives in the European Union, including beekeeping; (e) cooperation with specialized bodies to implement research programs in the field of beekeeping and beekeeping products; (f) market promotion, communication and marketing, including market monitoring, measures aimed at improving consumer awareness of the quality of beekeeping products; and (g) product quality improvement measures.

Policy: Government Decree No. HG204/2023 the Regulation on ecolabelling.
Policy_Content: Regulation on ecolabelling aims to create a voluntary ecolabelling system and promote on the market products and services with minimal environmental impact throughout their life cycle, compared to other products and services belonging to the same group of products and services. This Regulation establishes requirements for certification bodies in the field of ecolabelling, a procedure for checking the conformity of products and services, criteria for issuing an ecolabel, as well as a procedure for monitoring products and services with ecolabel. This Regulation does not apply to: (a) medicines for humans; (b) veterinary medicinal products; (c) medical products; (d) food products and feed; and (e) products containing substances, mixtures and preparations that meet the criteria for classification as toxic or hazardous to the environment. An ecolabel is a graphic symbol placed on a product, packaging, brochure or other information document that accompanies a product or service and provides the necessary information regarding the criteria for granting an ecolabel to products and services on the market. Ecolabelling certification bodies are private sector legal entities, independent and impartial, accredited by the National Accreditation Centre. If the ecolabelling certification body determines that a product or service do not meet the criteria for granting an ecolabel, or if the operator has not paid the product and service conformity testing fee, it will refuse to issue a certificate of conformity, giving reasons. The certificate of conformity is valid for 3 years with the possibility of extension for the same period. The criteria for granting an ecolabel are based on the environmental performance of the products and are established scientifically, taking into account the entire product life cycle.

Policy: Cabinet Regulation No. 184 validating the Procedure for obtaining and collecting information on the level of fertility of agricultural land and its changes, as well as recognizing providers of agrochemical soil research services.
Policy_Content: This Cabinet Regulation determines the Procedure for obtaining and collecting information on the level of fertility of agricultural land and its changes, as well as recognizing providers of agrochemical soil research services. The State Plant Protection Service obtains information in the following fields: (a) performing agrochemical research of soils; and (b) receiving soil agrochemical research data from recognized service providers. The fertility level of agricultural land is characterized by the following indicators: (a) soil type and granulometric composition; (b) humidity conditions; (c) terrain conditions; (d) degree of rockiness; and (e) agrochemical properties:  basic indicators – content of organic matter, exchange reaction (pH), content of phosphorus (P 2 O 5) and potassium (K 2 O) usable by plants; additional indicators – content of exchangeable magnesium (Mg), calcium (Ca), sulfur (S) and trace elements. Soil agrochemical research is a set of activities that includes the following stages: (a) development of field work plan projects using digitized soil maps; (b)  soil sampling according to the project of the field work plan; (c)  testing of agrochemical properties of soil samples in an accredited laboratory using soil testing methods published on the website of the service; (d) entering and maintaining the obtained data in the soil agrochemical research database of the Crop Monitoring State Information System of the Agricultural Land Management System; and (d) evaluation of the obtained data according to the evaluation groups of indicators of agrochemical properties of agricultural land ( Appendix 1 ). The Service creates a representative sample set of agricultural holdings in all state planning regions, using the following selection criteria: (a) state planning region; (b) county; and (c) farm specialization – agriculture, animal husbandry, horticulture – and farming system – organic or integrated.

Policy: Decree No. 11.471 establishing the National Council for the Rights of Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transvestite, Transgender, Queer, Intersex, Asexual and other People.
