The CNLGBTQIA+ aims to collaborate in the formulation of actions, guidelines and measures regarding lesbian, gay, bisexual, transvestite, transgender, queer, intersex, asexual and other people - LGBTQIA+. The CNLGBTQIA+ is responsible for: collaborating with the National Secretariat for the Rights of LGBTQIA+ People of the Ministry of Human Rights and Citizenship in elaborating criteria and parameters for governmental actions, at sectoral and cross-sectional levels, aimed at ensuring conditions of equality, equity and guaranteeing fundamental rights to LGBTQIA+ people; propose strategies for the evaluation and monitoring of government actions aimed at LGBTQIA+ people; monitor the preparation and execution of the Union's budget proposal, with the possibility of presenting recommendations regarding the allocation of resources, with a view to promoting and defending the rights of LGBTQIA+ people; legislative propositions that have implications for LGBTQIA+ people and present recommendations on said propositions; promote debates and research on the theme of rights and inclusion of LGBTQIA+ people; support campaigns aimed at promoting and defending rights and public policies for LGBTQIA+ people; organize the National LGBTQIA+ Conference and other nationwide events with an impact on LGBTQIA+ people; maintain exchanges at national and international entities, with a view to establishing common action strategies for the promotion and defense of rights and public policies in favor of LGBTQIA+ people, etc.

Policy_Content: The President, in order to increase the volume of food production through the efficient use of available resources, meet the needs of the population and maintain price stability in the domestic market, as well as economic and financial support for agricultural producers, decrees as follows: (a) from April 15, 2023, as an experiment, to introduce a new system for financing projects of initiators through the State Unitary Enterprise (SUE) "Agroservice operator" under the Agricultural Services Agency at the expense of attracted funds from international financial institutions, in accordance with which projects for the storage and processing of fruits and vegetables, the creation of logistics facilities, the purchase of grown products and special equipment, including the acquisition of technologies in the food industry, developed by the initiators, are submitted to the Agency's project offices in the regions and delivered to SUE "Agroservice operator" through the Unified Electronic information platform of the Ministry of Agriculture. The International Center for Strategic Development and Research in the Field of Food and Agriculture, in accordance with the established procedure, organizes the financing of projects. State Unitary Enterprise "Agroservice Operator" at the expense of these funds builds and leases to the initiators on a turnkey basis orchards and vineyards, agrologistic facilities, technological lines (modern greenhouses, laboratories, small agrologistic centers, processing facilities), lines in the food industry. At the same time, leasing is paid on the following terms: 10 percent - prepayment, 10 percent - the share of initiators, 80 percent - payment in installments over 10 years. The funds allocated under this procedure are provided in national currency at the rate of 14 percent per annum. Policy: Loi N°002-2023/ALT  portant renforcement de la neutralité politique et de la méritocratie dans l'Administration Publique.
Policy_Content: La présente loi a pour objet le renforcement de la neutralité politique et de la méritocratie dans l’Administration publique; ses dispositions s'appliquent aux agents publics. Il est interdit d’installer dans l’Administration publique, directement ou indirectement, de manière formelle ou informelle, des cellules ou toute forme de représentation de partis ou formations politiques. Les groupements à caractère religieux, ethnique ou régional à des fins politiques sont également interdits dans l’Administration publique. L’obligation de neutralité impose à l’agent public de s’abstenir, dans l’exercice ou à l’occasion de l’exercice de ses fonctions, de faire des distinctions de traitement entre les usagers suivant notamment leurs opinions, races, sexe ou d’user de son appartenance à l’Administration publique à des fins de propagande politique, idéologique, religieuse et ethnique.

Policy: Cabinet Regulation No. 163 amending Regulation No. 34 regarding emissions of pollutants into the aquatic environment.
Policy_Content: When carrying out emissions into water, shall be taken into account the environmental quality objectives specified in the Law on Water Management and water quality standards. If, in accordance with the Law "On Pollution", it is necessary to obtain a category A or category B permit for the emission of pollution into water, the State Environmental Service shall coordinate compliance of the permit conditions with the relevant environmental quality goals and water quality standards, as well as considering them when registering C-category polluting activities. In the application for obtaining a permit, including if significant changes in operations are planned, the operator, regardless of the type of wastewater discharge (into the environment, in a centralized sewage system or to external treatment facilities) must indicate the following information: (a) all priority substances or hazardous substances already used in the relevant facility or produced or created in the production process, as well as priority substances or hazardous substances contained in wastewater received from other operators, according to the information provided by the operators; (b) substances that the operator intends to use and which may occur in the process of polluting activity, if the polluting activity has not yet started or significant changes in the existing polluting activity are planned; (c) results of the operator's monitoring of polluting substances in wastewater; (d) the results of the initial mixing zone calculation in the receiving waters (surface waterbody) downstream discharge points of priority substances or hazardous substances, if the concentration of one or more of the mentioned substances in the discharged wastewater exceeds the environmental quality standards set in the water protection regulatory acts; and (e) the concentration of priority substances or hazardous substances found in wastewater as a result of measurements in the receiving waters upstream and downstream of the wastewater outlet.

Policy: Governmental Decree No. 532 validating the Regulation for the implementation of federal state control (supervision) in the field of seed production in relation to seeds of agricultural plants at checkpoints across the state border of the Russian Federation when importing seeds of agricultural plants into the Russian Federation from foreign states that are not members of the Eurasian Economic Union, and on amendments to Rules for exercising control over the passage of persons, vehicles, cargo, goods and animals across the state border of the Russian Federation.
Policy_Content: This Regulation establishes the procedure for the implementation of federal state control (supervision) in the field of seed production in relation to seeds of agricultural crops at checkpoints across the state border of the Russian Federations in the process of import of seeds of agricultural crops to the Russian Federation from foreign states that are not members of the Eurasian Economic Union. In the implementation of state control participate the Federal Service for Veterinary and Phytosanitary Supervision and its territorial bodies, as well as customs bodies. When exercising state control: (a) the compliance of imported seeds with the requirements for indicators of varietal and sowing (planting) qualities of seeds of agricultural plants established by the Ministry of Agriculture of the Russian Federation is assessed; (b) sampling (samples) of imported seeds is carried out for testing and (or) examinations, including for the presence of genetically modified organisms in imported seeds, in accordance with national and interstate standards. When exercising state control: (a) the compliance of imported seeds with the requirements for indicators of varietal and sowing (planting) qualities of seeds of agricultural crops established by the Ministry of Agriculture of the Russian Federation is assessed; and (b) sampling of imported seeds is carried out for testing and (or) examinations, including for the presence of genetically modified organisms in imported seeds, in accordance with national and interstate standards. When importing seeds into the customs territory of the Eurasian Economic Union, the carrier or a person acting on his behalf shall submit to the customs authority, along with the documents provided for by the Customs Code of the Eurasian Economic Union, the following documents: (a) the documents related to quality of imported seeds, with the exception of seeds of agricultural crops intended for use exclusively for carrying out examinations and research work; (b) genetic passports for varieties or hybrids of imported seeds that are included in the list of genera and species of agricultural crops; (c) documents containing information on chemical or biological preparations, pesticides used to treat imported seeds (in case of import of seeds treated with chemical or biological preparations, pesticides); (d) a copy of the contract (agreement) for the supply of seeds of agricultural crops for examinations (or) research work and (or) for educational purposes; and (e) an extract from the federal state information system in the field of seed production of agricultural crops confirming the intended use of imported seeds for examinations and research work, as well as for educational use.

Policy: Law No. LP71/2023 on subsidies for agriculture in rural areas.
Policy_Content: This Law establishes: (a) principles of state policy for subsidizing agriculture and rural areas; (b) powers of public authorities in the field of subsidizing agriculture and rural areas; (c) forms and conditions of subsidies for agriculture and rural areas; (d) particulars of the procedure for accepting and considering applications for subsidies. This Law does not regulate the principles of entrepreneurial activity, nor as well as the principles of the fiscal system of the Republic of Moldova. The objectives of this Law are: (a) increasing the competitiveness of the agro-industrial sector and its sustainable development; (b) ensuring sustainable management of natural resources; (c) sustainable socio-economic development of rural areas. To achieve the aforesaid objectives, the state supports: (a) modernization of the agri-food chain in order to comply with European Union food safety and quality requirements; (b) simplifying farmers’ access to markets for capital, means of production and finished products (input-output); (c) increasing added value in the agro-industrial sector through the development of primary and final processing infrastructure; (d) introduction of modern natural resource management practices; (e) introduction of production technologies that are favorable for the environment, ecological products, as well as the conservation of biological diversity; (f) adaptation to climate change and mitigation of its impacts on agricultural production; (g) development of infrastructure related to the availability and provision of services in rural areas; (h) expanding non-agricultural employment opportunities and increasing rural incomes; (i) balanced development of rural areas through the participation of local communities in rural development; and (j) development of micro, small and medium-sized farm enterprises. This Law contains VII Chapters divided into 34 Articles. Chapter I lays down general provisions. Chapter II establishes the principles of state policy for subsidizing agriculture and rural areas. Chapter III establishes powers of public bodies in the field of subsidizing agriculture and rural areas. Chapter IV regards National Fund of agricultural development and rural areas, and classifies the forms of subsidizing. Chapter V establishes acceptability conditions for subsidies and responsibilities of subsidizing entities. Chapter VI establishes the procedure for examination of applications for allocation of subsidies. Chapter VII lays down final and transitional provisions.

Policy: Complementary Law No. 1.037 reorganizes the organizational structure of the State Secretariat for the Environment and Water Resources (SEAMA).
Policy_Content: This Complementary Law, consisting of 41 articles and four Annexes, reorganizes the structure of the State Secretariat for the Environment and Water Resources (SEAMA). SEAMA, created under Law No. 3.043 of 31 December 1975, aims at managing public policies on the Environment and Water Resources and the management of tools to improve the sustainable development of Espírito Santo. In particular, SEAMA is responsible for: guide actions towards the sustainable use of natural resources and to improve the quality of life; propose, coordinate, manage and promote actions for the development of activities related to State Policies on the Environment, Environmental Education, Solid Waste Management, Climate Change, Conservation Units, Coastal Management and Water Resources, etc.; coordinate the elaboration of related guidelines; propose, support and supervise actions and the elaboration of research, scientific studies and projects aimed at conservation, recovery of environmental quality and improvement of quality of life; establish priority areas, with the objective of protecting or conserving natural resources; guide and support municipalities towards an integrated management of the Environment and Water Resources; promote the integration of activities related to the Environment and Water Resources protection; carry out research aimed at reducing the degradation of environmental quality; promote conservation of the State's environmental and landscape heritage; establish guidelines on to the State Policy on Environmental Education, etc.

Policy: Cabinet Regulation No. 144 on protected dendrological plantations.
Policy_Content: This Cabinet Regulation lists protected dendrological plantations. The boundaries of the dendrological plantations to be protected are determined in the Latvian geodetic coordinate system (LKS-92), which is determined as the coordinates of the Mercator transverse projection plane (LKS-92 TM), using as a cartographic basis an orthophoto map on a scale of 1:10,000, the data of the State Real Estate Cadastre Information System and Forest State Register data. The boundaries are determined without conducting an instrumental survey of the boundaries in the area. Until the instrumental survey of the boundaries in the area, deviations of the boundaries are allowed within the limits of certainty of the scale of the map used, according to the actual boundaries in nature. The geospatial data of the boundaries of protected dendrological plantations are available in the Natural Data Management System in accordance with the regulatory enactments on the procedure for maintaining the natural data management system, updating data and information circulation.

Policy: Regulation on good practice requirements in the field of forest management.
Policy_Content: This Regulation of the Minister of Climate and Environment, which is composed of four articles, lays down good practice requirements in the field of forest management used during the preparation and implementation of activities in the field of forest management. When preparing forest management activities, the forest owner or a person designated by him: (1) when planning forest management activities, take into account the need to maintain the diversity of development stages of forest stands in the forest; (2) review the available data to verify the presence of the species listed in Annex IV of Council Directive 92/43/EEC and the species of birds to be protected or their potential locations in the forest where the activities will be carried out; (3) carry out a site visit in the forest where these operations will be carried out in order to check the presence of species listed in Annex IV of Council Directive 92/43/EEC and protected bird species or potential places of their occurrence; (4) mark hollow trees, trees with bird nests with a diameter of more than 25 cm and other perennial nests.

Policy: Order No. 107/HK of the Minister of Digital Development, Innovation and Aerospace Industry of the Republic of Kazakhstan validating the Regulation for the creation and development of state geodetic, leveling and gravimetric networks.
Policy_Content: This Regulation establishes the procedure for the creation and development of state geodetic, leveling and gravimetric networks. State geodetic, leveling and gravimetric networks are a set of geodetic, leveling and gravimetric points located evenly throughout the territory of the Republic of Kazakhstan and fixed on the ground by special centers, ensuring their safety and stability in plan and height for a long time. The state geodetic networks of the Republic of Kazakhstan include permanent reference stations installed above the centers of points of the fundamental astronomical-geodetic network and high-precision geodetic network, based on the use of global navigation satellite systems in order to provide determination capabilities coordinates by consumers in near real time. The state geodetic networks (GGS) depending on the accuracy and other parameters of its constituent elements, methods and sequence of development, is structurally formed according to the principle of transition from the general to the specific and includes geodetic constructions of various accuracy classes: (a) fundamental astronomical and geodetic network; (b) high-precision geodetic network; (c) special satellite geodetic network; (d) satellite geodetic networks of class 1; and (e) precise geodetic networks.

Policy: Law No. 66 “On organic production”.
Policy_Content: This Law determines the legal framework for the activities of state bodies, subjects in the field of organic production and regulates relations regarding production, circulation, labelling of the following types of organic products: (a) products of animal and plant origin, including aquaculture and beekeeping; (b) processed products of agricultural origin; (c) feedstuffs; (d) vegetative seed material and seeds for cultivation; and (e) yeast used as a food or feed product; and (f) products collected and processed from forest, wild plants and planting materials. It shall not be applicable to the production, circulation and labelling of organic products produced for individual personal consumption, products of hunting (game) and fishing. State support of organic production shall be provided in the following fields: (a) formation, consulting and methodological support of organic production operators; (b) creation of competitive conditions for the increase of organic production and promotion of organic products in domestic and international markets; (c) provision of benefits technical assistance and other support to organic production operators exporting their products; (d) adoption of programs for the development and financing of organic production, including credits and non-repayable subsidies; (e) organizing training for organic production operators in skills and innovative technologies for organic production; (f) assistance in conducting scientific research in the field of organic production; (g) access to information and knowledge on organic production; (h) development of organic production; and (i) creation of conditions for providing access to organic production operators to production, natural resources and other means of production. Operators of organic production must comply with the following rules: (a) use for the purposes of organic production only healthy animals and plants, as well as safe products and raw materials of animal and plant origin; (b) implementation of organic production without the use of synthetic chemical fertilizers, pesticides, antibiotics, hormones, agrochemicals, with the exception of those included in the list of authorized substances approved by the authorized state body in the field of organic production; (c) ban on the use of chemically synthesized additives, except for those included in the list of authorized substances; (d) ban on the use of GMOs and products made from GMOs or with the use of GMOs; (e) ban on the use of hydroponic production methods using chemicals that are not included in the list of permitted substances; (f) ban on the use of ionizing radiation for the processing of organic food, feedstuffs or raw materials used in organic food or feedstuffs; (g) preservation and maintenance of soil fertility; (h) minimizing the use of non-renewable natural resources and means of production; (i) processing of waste and by-products of plant and animal origin, obtained in the conditions of organic production, for use in crop production and animal husbandry; (j) maintaining the ecological balance with organic production; (k) protection of plants using plant varieties that are not the result of biotechnology, means of biological control (entomophages, biological products), as well as using a properly organized crop rotation; (l) application of mechanical and physical protection methods of agricultural plants from pests, weeds and diseases; (m) care for the health of animals by stimulating the natural immune defense of their body; (n) selection of animal breeds, taking into account the possibility and degree of their adaptation to local conditions, viability and resistance to diseases; (o) use of livestock grown in condition of organic production; (p) use of feedstuffs containing only agricultural ingredients of organic production; (q) conservation of biological diversity of natural aquatic ecological systems; and (r) creation of a buffer zone to protect against air and water pollution. This Law contains 9 Chapters divided into 34 articles. Chapter 1 lays down general provisions. Chapter 2 establishes rules for organic production. Chapter 3 regards certification of organic production. Chapter 4 regards labelling of organic production. Chapter 5 regards import and export of organic products. Chapter 6 establishes competence of state bodies in the field of organic production. Chapter 7 establishes rights and obligations of subjects of organic production. Chapter 8 establishes the responsibility for violation of legislation in the field of organic production. Chapter 9 lays down final provisions.

Policy_Content: This Decree creates the National Council for Sustainable Rural Development (Condraf), under the Ministry of Agrarian Development and Family Agriculture. Policy: Regulation on the good agricultural practice code.
Policy_Content: This Regulation prescribes the code of good agricultural practice. The code of good agricultural practice is the application of knowledge in the use of natural resources, i.e. a set of rules that is directly applied by the owner or user of agricultural land with the aim of maintaining agricultural land suitable for agricultural production and sustainable in terms of necessary grade of environmental protection that has to be applied. The owner, that is, the user of agricultural land, maintains the agricultural land suitable for agricultural production and protects the environment by applying agro-technical and amelioration measures with the aim of: 1) maintaining the fertility of agricultural land; 2) prevention of degradation of agricultural land and protection against erosion; 3) reduction of greenhouse gas emissions caused by agricultural production; 4) reducing the risk of contamination of agricultural land and groundwater with pollutants from agricultural production with nitrates and phosphates, originating from plant nutrition; 5) preventing the appearance of abandoned agricultural land; 6) preservation of landscape features; 7) correct use of land temporarily prohibited for agricultural production and its marking.

The Aquilomba Brasil Programme will be coordinated by the Ministry of Racial Equality. The principles of the Programme are: transversality of gender and race in public policies aimed at the quilombola population; respect for self-determination, territorial integrity and the full effectiveness of the social, economic and cultural rights of the quilombola population, recognized in the Constitution and in Convention No. 169 of the International Labour Organization; recognition of the traditional quilombola way of life as a sustainable practice of relating to nature; prioritization of assistance to quilombola communities in situations of social vulnerability, where there are significant rates of violence and low levels of education; social participation and control in public policies for the quilombola population; gender equity; and government actions to implement the rights of the quilombola population. The Programme will include also actions aimed at the following thematic axes: access to land and territory; infrastructure and quality of life; productive inclusion and local development; and rights and citizenship.

Policy: Law No. 1955 “On public procurement”.
Policy_Content: This Law defines the organizational, legal and economic foundations of public procurement and is aimed at creating a unified public procurement system that ensures the efficient and economical use of public funds based on the principles of competition, fair treatment of all participants in the competition and transparency of the public procurement procedure. Public procurement (purchases) shall be intended the acquisition by a procuring organization of goods, works and services, financed in the manner prescribed by this Law, in whole or in part from public funds. Procurement contract shall be intended an agreement concluded upon completion of public procurement procedures for goods, works and services. Goods shall be intended products of any type and purpose, including raw materials, products, equipment, technology, objects in solid, liquid and gaseous states, electrical and thermal energy, objects of ownership in accordance with the legislation of the Republic of Tajikistan, as well as services related to the supply goods, if the cost of such services does not exceed the goods. Public procurement is based on the following principles: (a) rational use of public funds, economy and efficiency in public procurement; (b) competition within transparent public procurement procedures; (c) equality and fair treatment of all participants in the competition, as well as suppliers (contractors) executing public procurement contracts; and (d) confidentiality of information containing state or other secret protected by law. The following purchasing organizations are participants in public procurement: (a) budgetary institutions; (b) government bodies; (c) state enterprises; (d) organizations and institutions formed by the Government of the Republic of Tajikistan, government and administrative bodies; (e) public utilities financed from the local or republican budget; (f) self-government bodies of towns and villages; (g) state trust funds; (h) joint-stock companies and other business entities in which more than 50 percent of shares or shares belong to the state; (i) bodies of state power and administration, state organizations, institutions or enterprises that manage funds received into their accounts from the owners of these funds; (j) branches and (or) representative offices of the above legal entities; and (k) state banks. Purchasing organizations, in accordance with regulatory legal acts, apply measures that contribute to sustainable and social development of the Republic of Tajikistan. A framework of rules and practices for procurement for sustainable and social development may include elements such as reducing negative impacts and promoting potential positive environmental impacts of procurement expenditures, enhancing opportunities for small and medium-sized enterprises.

Policy: Loi n°2023-004 du 13 mars 2023 portant Code des Collectivités territoriales.
Policy_Content: Cette loi contient le Code des Collectivités Territoriales, notamment la Commune et la Région. La Commune est une collectivité territoriale dotée de la personnalité morale et de l’autonomie financière; elle est urbaine ou rurale. La Commune urbaine se compose essentiellement de quartiers; la Commune rurale se compose essentiellement de villages et/ou de fractions. Policy: Regulation on the criteria for recognizing agricultural land as being in a state that makes it suitable for grazing or cultivation.
Policy_Content: This Regulation of the Minister of Agriculture and Rural Development lays down the criteria for recognizing agricultural land as being in a state that makes it suitable for grazing or cultivation. Agricultural land is considered to be in a condition that makes it suitable for grazing or cultivation if: (1) at least one agrotechnical operation has been carried out to remove or destroy undesirable vegetation - in the case of arable land and permanent grassland ; (2) at least two agricultural treatments have been carried out including one aimed at removing or destroying undesirable vegetation and the other aimed at removing dead trees or branches, or sanitary pruning of dry and drying branches - in the case of orchards.

Policy: Regulation on standards and detailed conditions for their use.
Policy_Content: This Regulation of the Minister of Agriculture and Rural Development lays down standards and detailed conditions for their use considering the criteria specified in art.13 point 1 of the Regulation (EU) 2021/2115. In particular arable land is not burned, but for reasons related to plant health, it is allowed to burn plants, parts of plants or post-harvest residues. Fertilizers are not applied on arable land located within 3 m from the shores of lakes and water reservoirs other than lakes. Arable land located on slopes with a slope of at least 14% is not used for the cultivation of plants requiring the maintenance of ridges along the slope. The protective soil cover is maintained at least from November 1 of a given year to February 15 of the following year on an area of at least 80% of the arable land included in the farm and in the inter-rows of fruit tree plantations.

Policy: The Agricultural Wages (Wales) Order 2023.
Policy_Content: This Order revokes and replaces the Agricultural Wages (No. 2) (Wales) Order 2022. Part 2 of the Order provides for terms and condition of employment for agricultural workers and specifies the different grades and categories of agricultural worker (article 5 to 9). Part 3 makes provision about the minimum rates of pay, minimum rates of pay for overtime, for output work, identifies payments which do not form part of an agricultural worker’s remuneration. The Part also grants a protection of pay to agricultural workers employed before a certain date who suffered a reduction in their minimum hourly rate as a result of their assimilation to a lower grade or category or a lower minimum rate of pay as specified in the Table in Schedule 1 of the Agricultural Wages (Wales) Order 2022. Part 4 provides that an agricultural worker is entitled to agricultural sick pay in the circumstances specified (articles 18 to 21).  Part 5 makes provision about an agricultural worker’s entitlement to time off. Provision is made about an agricultural worker’s entitlement to rest breaks (article 28), daily rest (article 29 ) and weekly rest period (article 30). Provision is also made specifying the agricultural worker’s annual leave year and about the agricultural worker’s entitlement to annual leave, holiday pay and about payment in lieu of annual leave (articles 31 to 38). Provision about an agricultural worker’s entitlement to be paid bereavement leave is made in articles 41 to 43.

Policy: Minister of the Environment Decision No. 80 of 2023 regarding the Supreme Committee for Compensation.
Policy_Content: This Resolution, comprising 13 articles, outlines the following key provisions: (i) The Chief Executive Officer of the Environmental Affairs Agency will lead the restructured Supreme Compensation Committee, tasked with establishing scientific foundations for determining environmental compensation values resulting from activity violations. The committee reviews grievances and adopts estimated compensation values assessed by the Technical Secretariat for Compensations. (ii) The restructured Technical Secretariat Committee for Compensations, now the “Technical Secretariat Committee for Compensations and Grievances,” is led by the Head of the Environmental Management Sector. Serving as an assistant to the Supreme Compensation Committee, it is responsible for tasks such as studying technical reports, estimating initial environmental damage, presenting opinions to the Supreme Committee, notifying concerned parties, receiving and examining grievances, preparing for Supreme Committee meetings, documenting decisions, and coordinating with relevant authorities. The committee also prepares model letters and a grievance model for approval by the Supreme Compensation Committee. (iii) A specialized team, led by the head of the Technical Secretariat and Grievances Committee, is formed to assess environmental damage cases, particularly those from urgent situations and incidents of marine and river pollution involving petroleum oil, derivatives, and harmful substances. The team, including representatives from the Technical Secretariat Committee and a member from the Central Administration for Crises and Disasters, presents its findings directly to the Higher Accreditation Committee.

Policy: Law No. LP43/2023 on fluorinated greenhouse gases.
Policy_Content: This Law transposes the Regulations (EC) of the European Parliament and Council No. 517/2014 of April 16, 2014 on fluorinated greenhouse gases. This law establishes the legal basis for the implementation of measures relating to both climate change mitigation and environmental protection by reducing fluorinated greenhouse gas emissions. The scope of this Law is to regulate at the national level precautionary measures regarding: (a) prevention of leakage, use, recovery and disposal of fluorinated greenhouse gases, as well as those associated with the listed supporting measures; (b) placement on the market of individual products and equipment containing fluorinated greenhouse gases or those operating on their basis, with the exception of refrigeration and/or air conditioning equipment that does not currently contain such gases at the moment of import; (c) special use of fluorinated greenhouse gases; and (d) application of quantitative restrictions for placing on the market of hydrofluorocarbons. This Law establishes standards, conditions and restrictions, applicable to the following fluorinated greenhouse gases: (a) hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs), used as refrigerants, cleaning solvents and foaming agents, including those used in fire extinguishers; (b) perfluorocarbons (PFCs) used in semiconductor production, as cleaning solvents and foaming agents; (c) sulfur hexafluoride (SF6), used in high voltage electrical installations and in the production of magnesium. The provisions of this Law apply to refrigeration, air conditioning equipment, other equipment, installations and products, containing or operating on the basis of fluorinated greenhouse gases. In order to implement this law, the following principles shall be complied with: (a) the principle of “green chemistry”, also called the principle of “sustainable chemistry”, by promoting measures that contribute to the reduction or elimination of emissions of fluorinated gases; (b) the principle of extended responsibility of the manufacturer and/or the end consumer - by establishing the obligation to both to eliminate leaks of fluorinated gases and their recovery, recirculation, regeneration or disposal; (c) the principle of pollution prevention; (d) the precautionary principle in decision making; (e) the “polluter pays” principle; (f) the principle of transparency and accessibility; and (g) the principle of motivation to learn. The release of fluorinated gases into the atmospheric air is prohibited, if such emission is not a technical condition for its intended use. Import, export, re-export and transit of each lot of fluorinated gases, specified in Annex 1, as well as products and equipment containing fluorinated greenhouse gases or those operating on their basis are carried out in accordance with a permit issued by the Environment Agency. This Law contains VIII Chapters divided into 39 Articles. Chapter I lays down general provisions. Chapter II establishes powers and obligations. Chapter III regards prevention of leakages. Chapter IV regards placing on the market and regulation of use. Chapter V regards limitation of the quantity of hydrofluorocarbons placed on the market. Chapter VI regards information and reporting. Chapter VII establishes competence in the process of control performance and liability for the infringement of legislation in the field of reducing fluorinated greenhouse gases emissions. Chapter VIII lays down final and transitional provisions.

Policy: Regulation (EU) 2021/241 establishing the Recovery and Resilience Facility.
Policy_Content: This Regulation establishes the Recovery and Resilience Facility and lays down the objectives of the Facility, its financing, and the forms of Union funding and its provision. In the context of the COVID-19 crisis, the Facility shall promote the Union’s economic, social and territorial cohesion by improving the resilience, crisis preparedness, adjustment capacity and growth potential of the Member States, by mitigating the social and economic impact of that crisis, in particular on women. The Facility shall be implemented by the Commission referring to EU policies in the fields of: (I) green transition; (II) digital transformation; (III) smart, sustainable and inclusive growth, including economic cohesion, jobs, productivity, competitiveness, research, development and innovation, and a well-functioning internal market with strong small- and medium-scale enterprises; (IV) social and territorial cohesion; (V) health, and economic, social and institutional resilience, with the aim of increasing crisis preparedness and crisis response capacity; and (VI) policies for the next generation, children and the youth, such as education and skills. Member States shall prepare national recovery and resilience plans in this scope and necessary financial support shall be provided by the Facility from the Union funds. Support under the Facility shall be additional to the support provided under other Union programmes and instruments. The Commission shall monitor the implementation of the Facility and the monitoring of implementation shall be targeted and proportionate to the activities carried out under the Facility.

Policy: Law No. ZRU-819 “On technical regulation”.
Policy_Content: The scope of this Law is to regulate relations in the field of technical regulation. This Law applies to relationships arising from the development, adoption and application of technical regulations, conformity assessment and implementation of state control in the field of technical regulation. This Law does not apply to the following relations: (a) sanitary, phytosanitary and veterinary measures; (b)  measures in the field of labor protection; and (c) standards of healthcare. Technical regulation shall be intended establishment, application and compliance with product safety requirements, processes and methods of its production, as well as verification of their compliance by evaluating compliance and implementation of state control. The main principles of technical regulation are: (a) unity of application of technical regulations; (b) inadmissibility of discrimination of business entities and unfair competition in the field of technical regulation; (c) unity and integrity of technical regulation and evaluation compliance; (d) independence of conformity assessment bodies from manufacturers, sellers and buyers (consumers); (e) unity of rules and methods of testing and measurement during mandatory conformity assessment procedures; (f) inadmissibility of combining powers by one body on state control and confirmation of conformity; and (g) inadmissibility of duplication of the same powers by two and more government control bodies. State regulation in the field of technical regulation shall be performed by: (a) Cabinet of Ministers and government agencies; (b) state technical regulation bodies; (c) authorized state bodies in the field of technical regulation; (d) state national standardization body; (e) accreditation body; and (f) technical expert commissions in the field of technical regulation, conformity assessment bodies, testing laboratories. The main directions of state policy in the field of technical regulation are: (a) ensuring compliance of technical regulation with the level of development of the economy, material and technical base, as well as the level scientific and technological development; (b) development and implementation of development programs in this field; (c) harmonization of this field with international (regional) standards; (d) introduction of advanced communication technologies; innovative and improvement of the training system, and advanced training of personnel; and (e) development of international cooperation. Technical regulations are adopted in order to: (a) protect life or health of citizens by establishing product safety requirements; (b) protect environment, flora and fauna; (c) prevent actions that mislead buyers (consumers); (c) ensure energy efficiency and rational use of natural resources; (d) prevent technical barriers to trade; and (e) increase the competitiveness of products in the domestic and foreign markets.

Policy: Investment Act, No. 10 of 2022.
Policy_Content: This Act, comprising 37 Articles divided into five Parts, aims to create a favourable environment for investments in Tanzania. It establishes conditions for business enterprises to be eligible for certain benefits and protections. To qualify, a business must meet specific requirements and cannot engage in activities related to mining, petroleum, hazardous chemicals, armaments, or explosives. The minimum investment capital needed depends on ownership status. Under Article 4 there shall continue to exist the Tanzania Investment Centre a one-stop centre for investors and the government's primary agency to coordinate, encourage, promote and facilitate investment and advise the Government on investment policy and related matters. All requests for certificates of incentives and protection under this Act, or to rehabilitate or expand an existing enterprise, must be submitted to the Centre, which will issue these certificates by the Regulations. The Centre shall maintain a register of all certified business enterprises containing such particulars as the Board may determine. Furthermore, a National Investment Steering Committee shall be established to effectively promote, facilitate, and implement investment projects in Tanzania. By the provision of Article 23, notable strategic investments shall be recognised and granted additional benefits. The article also indicates the cases in which a business enterprise is regarded as a strategic investment.

Policy: Presidential Decree No. UP-24 “On additional measures to protect pastures and ensure their rational use”.
Policy_Content: The President, in order to protect pastures, ensure their rational use, as well as further development of ferula cultivation and the widespread use of resource-saving technologies in pastures appoints Committee for the development of sericulture and wool industry under the Ministry of Agriculture responsible body in the field of use and protection of pastures belonging thereto. The Committee on its pastures must to take the following measures: (a) the use and protection of pastures, including the organization and control of the rational and targeted use of pastures by users, regardless of their form of ownership; (b) the development of ferula cultivation, the effective use of wild ferula, as well as the preservation of its distribution areas and the increase in ferula cultural plantations; and (c) implementation of state control and effective management in the use of pastures. There shall be established the procedure in accordance with which, when creating ferula cultural plantations, periodic monitoring shall be carried out by the Committee within two years from the date of registration of planting acts, and based on the results of monitoring, the plant germination area is entered by the Ministry of Natural Resources into the state register as a plantation. In order to ensure the natural population, reproduction and restoration of the Tajik ferula plant, listed in the Red Book of the Republic of Uzbekistan, shall be applied a moratorium on the use of Tajik ferula for a period of three years starting from this year. The Committee, together with the Ministry of Natural Resources and ministries and departments concerned, should take appropriate measures for the use without permits (extraction from nature, collection, felling, damage, destruction) and sale on land under its jurisdiction of all types of ferula plants included and not included in Red Data Book of the Republic of Uzbekistan.

Policy_Content: The President, in order to widely introduce renewable energy sources in the social sphere, housing and communal services and sectors of the economy, to ensure compensation for the energy shortage in the regions by improving energy efficiency, comprehensive organization of work in this field, as well as creating favorable conditions and introducing incentive mechanisms for investors, decrees as follows: (a) to support the proposals of the Ministry of Energy, the Ministry of Economy and Finance, as well as the Ministry of Investment, Industry and Trade, providing for in 2023 commissioning of renewable energy sources with a total capacity of 4,300 MW, including large solar and wind power plants with a capacity of 2,100 MW, solar panels installed on buildings and structures of social facilities and business entities, households with a capacity of 1,200 MW, small photovoltaic stations built by entrepreneurs - with a capacity of 550 MW; (b) to ensure production of an additional 5 billion kilowatt/hour of electrical energy and saving 4.8 billion cubic meters of natural gas in 2023 through the construction of renewable energy installations, the transfer of consumers to alternative energy and the introduction of energy-saving technologies; and (c) to guarantee allocation of funds for these purposes in the amount of a total of 15.4 billion US dollars, including funds of investors within the framework of public-private partnership projects - 13.4 billion US dollars, loans from commercial banks - 1.1 billion US dollars, own funds enterprises - 610 million US dollars, funds of foreign financial organizations - 150 million US dollars, funds of the State budget in the equivalent of 100 million US dollars. Starting from April 1, 2023, natural persons and legal entities that have installed renewable energy sources installations with a total capacity of up to 100 kW are exempt from paying property tax - according to these installations, land tax - for plots occupied by these installations, income tax - accrued on profit for electricity sold by legal entities for the general grid, from the date of their commissioning - for a period of three years, in case of their installation with an electric energy storage system with a capacity of at least 25 percent of the capacity of installed solar panels - for a period of up to ten years. Starting from March 1, 2023, when connecting to the electric grid installations of renewable energy sources that do not exceed the capacity specified in the technical specifications issued for connection to the unified electric power system, no additional technical specification is required.

Policy_Content: This Regional Law establishes in Moscow region the requirements, under which the territory of performance of gardening or gardening by citizens for their own needs can be included in the boundaries of the settlement or within the boundaries of the territory of gardening can be formed a new settlement. Territories of gardening can be included in the boundaries of the settlement subject to the following requirements: (a) the presence of a common boundary with the settlement; (b) the area of the annexed territory, with the exception of clusters of individual housing construction, cannot exceed the area of the locality to which it joins; (c) the number of land plots with residential buildings should be at least 50 percent of the total number of land plots; (d) the presence of a decision of the general meeting of members of the horticultural non-profit partnership, horticultural or suburban non-profit partnerships on the inclusion of the territory within the boundaries of the settlement; (e) compliance with urban design standards of Moscow region to provide the planned population with facilities of social, transport, engineering infrastructure. Horticultural areas can be included in the boundaries of a locality in case of change of the type of authorized use of land plots for "gardening". Inclusion in the boundaries of the settlement of individual land plots of horticultural or gardening areas is not allowed.

Policy: Law No. HO-11-N “On genetically modified organisms”.
Policy_Content: This Law regulates genetically modified organisms in the Republic of Armenia, including acceptance, import, testing, storage, management, application, examination, transportation, destruction, adverse effects on the environment, human health, biodiversity and in connection with ensuring biosecurity and protection of agricultural land. The purpose of this law is to prevent the violation of biosafety principles of the use of GMOs. Genetically modified organisms (GMOs) (obtained by genetic engineering, transgenic) shall be intended an organism or several organisms, any non-cellular, single-celled or a multicellular organism capable of reproducing or transmitting hereditary genetic material that differentiates are obtained from natural organisms using genetic engineering methods and contain genetic engineering material, including genes, parts thereof or combinations of genes. Biosecurity related to the use of GMOs shall be intended a set of measures that guarantees the exclusion of any adverse effects of GMOs on the environment, human health and biodiversity. The sphere of application of this Law extends to agriculture, healthcare, environment applicable to processes related to the use of GMOs and biosecurity. In the Republic of Armenia, the use of GMOs intended for reproduction or their use in any other way is prohibited, except for those used by scientific research organizations in an isolated system in accordance with the requirements set by the Government for scientific research and demonstration purposes. Plant organisms intended for reproduction imported for the purpose of identifying GMOs are subject to laboratory examination by the authorized state body carrying out border control. The list of plant species subject to laboratory examination is determined by the Government. GMOs imported to the Republic of Armenia for research and demonstration purposes must be accompanied by a contract signed between the producing and importing organizations, specifying the use of GMO for scientific research and demonstration purposes. Each process involving the use of GMO shall be subject to monitoring.

Policy: Regional Law No. 5-RZ “On regulation of some issues in the field of apiculture development.”
Policy_Content: This Regional Law regulates some issues in the field of apiculture development. Policy: Resolution No. 112 of the Cabinet of Ministers validating the Procedure for the performance of forest management.
Policy_Content: This Procedure defines a unified system and conditions for the organization and implementation of forest management. System and conditions of organization and implementation of forest management shall be intended a set of measures that determine the conditions and mechanism of implementation of forest management and organization of relations with participants in the forest management process. The main components of the forest management system are: (a) determination of the conditions and mechanism of forest management in accordance with Article 46 of the Forest Code of Ukraine; and (b) organization of relations between the state forest management organization and permanent forest users, citizens and legal entities that own forests in private ownership, - in terms of the performance of duties related to forestry management based on forest management materials in accordance with Articles 14 and 19 of the Forest Code of Ukraine; by the State Forestry Agency and its territorial bodies - in terms of the organization of forest management in accordance with Article 28-1 of the Forest Code of Ukraine; by state authorities and local self-government bodies - in terms of their implementation of state policy in the field of forest relations in accordance with Articles 30 and 31 of the Forest Code of Ukraine, in particular regarding the development of programs for the protection, protection, use and reproduction of forests. Forest management is carried out by state forest management organizations. The objects of forest management are forest plots and non-forest land, which are provided for use or ownership in accordance with the established procedure and are used for the needs of forestry. Forest management is classified into primary basic and secondary basic. Changes may be made to the materials of the primary basic and secondary basic forest management for the purpose of maintaining up-to-date inventory and cartographic databases, which contain quantitative and qualitative information about forest areas, and for the purpose of producing up-to-date forest management materials. Primary basic forest management is carried out in forests that are managed for the first time. Repeated basic forest management is carried out in previously managed forests. The relationship of the state forest management organization with the territorial bodies of the State Forestry Agency and permanent forest users (forest owners) is determined by contracts for forest management works and decisions of forest management meetings. State forest management organizations cooperate with executive authorities, local self-government bodies, participate in the development of programs for the guardianship, protection, use and reproduction of forests, involve the public and other interested parties at all stages of forest management.

Policy: Climate Protection and Climate Adaptation Act (KlimaG BW).
Policy_Content: The Law encompasses various provisions and objectives aimed at making a significant contribution to climate protection and coping with the inevitable consequences of climate change. The Law provides a hierarchy for climate protection ranging as: (1) avoiding greenhouse gas emissions, (2) reducing greenhouse gas emissions, and (3) sequestering greenhouse gases that cannot be avoided or reduced with reasonable effort.  The law emphasizes the preservation, protection, and establishment of natural carbon sinks to contribute to climate protection and resilience. In chapter 2 the Law sets sectoral targets and goals for state administration, and objectives for municipal administrations for climate protection. Public authorities are tasked with a general role model function in climate action, prioritizing measures according to the climate hierarchy within their organizational scope and there exists an obligation to consider climate aspects in planning and decision-making processes. It also establishes funding programs to support measures for climate protection and adaptation. In Chapter 4 the text provides for conservation of energy, promotion of renewable energies through ensuring availability of land, and installation of photovoltaic systems and distribution networks. Final Chapter provides for the administration process, monitoring and financial compensation.

Policy: Law No. 5 of 2023 establishing the Dubai Corporation for Consumer Protection and Fair Trade (DCCPFT).
Policy_Content: This Law comprising 25 articles, establishes in the Emirate of Dubai the Dubai Corporation for Consumer Protection and Fair Trade (DCCPFT) with the following main objectives (i) to contribute to the creation of a stimulating investment environment based on fair trade and legitimate competition; (ii) to ensure the economic stability by protecting consumer rights and promoting the interests of the business sector; (iii) to enhance the competitiveness of business practices and curb harmful negative practices, such as restrictive agreements, unfair exploitation, dominant positions, and economic concentration; (iv) to improve the system of commercial control processes in all economic sectors to promote the highest interests of the Emirate; (v) to standardize and streamline commercial control processes in local markets. The DCCPFT will have the general duties and powers to (i) developing strategic plans and general policies for upholding the principles of Competition and Fair Trade, protecting the rights of Consumers and of the business sector, and curbing Economic Concentration;  (ii) implementing the policies, programs, and initiatives aimed at protecting consumer rights and accomplishing fair trade; (iii) reviewing and proposing the legislation related to consumer protection, fair trade, and competitiveness promotion; (iv) protecting intellectual property rights, raising the business sector’s awareness of the importance of registering the same and ways of protecting them, and considering complaints related to the violation of these rights; (v) supporting and stimulating the business environment in the Emirate; (vi) determining the complaints filed with it by Commercial Establishments or Consumers, and mediating amicable settlements between the parties to these complaints; (vii) organizing awareness campaigns on Consumer rights, Fair Trade, and legitimate Competition; (viii) regulating the pricing of commodities and services in times of emergencies, crises, and disasters; (ix) cooperating and coordinating with other Regulatory Bodies to enhance the competitiveness and the investment environment of the Emirate, and unifying inspection operations and procedures; (x) holding trade exhibitions and events related to Consumer protection, Fair Trade, and Commercial Control.

Policy: Resolution No. 105 of the Cabinet of Ministers validating the Procedure for felling trees and shrubs and using the extracted timber in the event of a change in the purpose of forest land plots or the establishment of servitude for their use for purposes not related to forestry management, and transfer of forest land to non-forest land.
Policy_Content: This Procedure establishes the requirements for felling trees and shrubs and using the extracted timber in the event of a change in the purpose of forest land plots or the establishment of servitude for their use for purposes not related to forestry management, and transfer of forest land to non-forest land. The effect of this Resolution does not apply to the harvesting of timber during felling for main use, maintenance, sanitary, reforestation, reshaping, landscape and felling related to reconstruction. In the event of a decision to change the intended use of land and forest plots in order to use them for purposes not related to forestry management, the bodies that make such a decision simultaneously decide on the issue of preserving or felling trees and shrubs and on the procedure for use of wood obtained at the same time. In the event of a decision to change the intended purpose of land forest plots for the purpose of their use for purposes not related to forestry management, with the right to cut down trees and shrubs, timber harvesting is carried out by those citizens and legal entities to whom they are transferred into ownership or provided for use such land plots, unless otherwise provided by the said decision. At the same time, the right of ownership of harvested timber and income from its sale is held by citizens and legal entities to whom ownership of such plots of land has been transferred or provided for use. In the event of a decision to change the purpose of forest land plots for the purpose of their use for purposes not related to forestry management, with the right to cut down trees and shrubs, which is granted to a permanent forest user, the owner of forests, the right to harvest timber, the right to own harvested timber and income from its sale belong to the forest owner, a permanent forest user. In the event of a decision to change the purpose of land forest plots for the purpose of their use for purposes not related to forestry management, without the right to cut down trees and shrubs, citizens and legal entities to whom land forest plots are transferred to ownership or provided for use, are obliged to ensure the preservation and care of trees and shrubs.

Policy: Ley Orgánica De Transparencia Y Acceso a la Información Pública.
Policy_Content: La presente Ley tiene por objeto garantizar y regular el derecho de acceso a la información pública en cumplimiento de la Constitución de la República del Ecuador, la ley; y de los instrumentos internacionales ratificados por el Estado ecuatoriano. La finalidad es proteger, respetar, promover y garantizar que la información pública sea accesible, oportuna, completa y fidedigna, para el ejercicio de los derechos ciudadanos. En el ejercicio del derecho de acceso a la información pública se observarán prioritariamente los siguientes enfoques: 1) Derechos Humanos (considera a las personas como sujetos de derechos con dignidad, identificando las relaciones de poder que condicionan y limitan el ejercicio del derecho humano de acceso a la información pública); 2) Género (debe existir la responsabilidad de los sujetos obligados para garantizar el derecho de aquellas que quieren acceder conforme sus particularidades); 3) Intergeneracional (considera las capacidades y necesidades físicas, sociales y culturales con relación al ciclo de vida de las personas); 4) Inclusivo (considera las desigualdades que inciden en la exclusión social como los recursos económicos y conocimientos, para promover la inclusión de las personas mediante el uso de mecanismos digitales y no digitales).

Policy: Decree No. 50 of the Cabinet of Ministers validating the Regulation on the procedure for monitoring, evaluating and developing reporting forms for combating land degradation and publishing their results.
Policy_Content: The Regulation on the procedure for monitoring, evaluation and reporting forms of measures to combat land degradation, as well as publishing their results, provides for the following: (a) the procedure for organizing monitoring of measures to combat land degradation and receiving reports; (b) procedure for publishing the results of measures to combat land degradation; and (c) procedure for using materials on land degradation, desertification and drought, and measures taken to combat it. The Ministry of Agriculture, together with the Ministry of Digital Technologies, shall develop the "Land Degradation" geo-information portal on the basis of the integrated unified information system of the Ministry of Agriculture in order to create an information base related to land degradation, drought and desertification, measures to combat them, by June 1, 2023 and put it into practice. This Regulation is aimed at mitigating the negative consequences of land degradation, global climate change, drought and desertification, maintaining, increasing and restoring soil fertility on agricultural land, providing information exchange between ministries and agencies in this regard, and combating degradation. determines the procedure for carrying out activities, developing report forms and publishing their results. The Ministry of Agriculture of the Republic of Uzbekistan, in order to maintain a unified state policy in the field of combating the processes of land degradation, to develop state programs and prospective strategies for combating the processes of land degradation, shall coordinate the activities of ministries and agencies participating in their implementation. The responsible ministries and agencies regularly enter information on land degradation and measures to combat it into the electronic map of the "Land Degradation Geoinformation System" (based on layers and attributes). These data are included in the WGS-84 coordinate system on the basis of uniform classifications in accordance with the regulations approved by the Ministry of Agriculture. According to the results of monitoring and soil research, the level of degradation of land areas is estimated as follows: land structure intact (ETB); disturbed by anthropogenic influence (ATB); not degraded (DU); weakly degraded (KzD); medium degraded (O'D); strongly degraded (KD); highly degraded (O'KD). In the digital maps of the "Land Degradation Geo-Information System", the degraded lands are separated according to the above assessment levels and displayed with the appropriate colors and conventional symbols.

Policy: Regulation on the export and import of certain hazardous chemicals.
Policy_Content: The objectives of this Regulation are to: (I) implement the Rotterdam Convention on the Prior Informed Consent Procedure for Certain Hazardous Chemicals and Pesticides in International Trade (the ‘Con­vention’); (II) promote shared responsibility and cooperative efforts in the international movement of hazardous chemicals in order to protect human health and the environment from potential harm; (III) contribute to the environmentally sound use of hazardous chemicals; (IV) facilitate the exchange of information concerning the characteristics of hazardous chemicals; and (V) provide for a decision-making process on the import and export of hazardous chemicals and disseminate decisions to Parties and other countries as appropriate. This Regulation shall apply to certain hazardous chemicals that are banned or severely restricted and listed in Annex-1, and certain hazardous chemicals that are subject to the prior informed consent procedure under the Convention and listed in Annex-2. This Regulation shall not apply to: radioactive materials and substances; wastes; chemical substances and mixtures used in the manufacture of chemical weapons; medicinal products for human or veterinary use; food and food additives; feedingstuffs for animals; narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances; and genetically modified organisms. This Regulation has been drafted in line with the Regulation (EU) No. 649/2012 of 4 July 2012 concerning the export and import of hazardous chemicals.

Policy: Ley Nº 6977 - Que regula el fomento, generación, producción, desarrollo y la utilización de energía eléctrica a partir de fuentes de energías renovables no convencionales no hidráulicas.
Policy_Content: La presente Ley consta de 52 artículos y tiene por objeto promover el fomento, generación, producción, desarrollo y la utilización de energía eléctrica a partir del uso de fuentes de energías renovables no convencionales (ERNC) no hidráulicas. Las ERNC son las fuentes de energías no fósiles: biomasa, bioenergía, geotérmica, solar, eólica, e hidrógeno verde. La producción de energía a partir de ERNC solo podrá ser realizada par personas físicas o jurídicas con domicilio en el país, constituidas de acuerdo con la legislación vigente, las que requerirán de una licencia otorgada por la autoridad de aplicación. La Ley declara las actividades de producción y utilización de ERNC como un asunto de utilidad pública e interés social fundamental para asegurar la diversificación del abastecimiento energético, la protección del ambiente, el uso eficiente de la energía y la preservación y conservación de los recursos naturales renovables, otorgándosele beneficios tributarios a las personas que realicen dichas actividades. El ámbito de aplicación de la ley son aquellas actividades generadoras de energía eléctrica a partir de fuentes de ERNC, la producción y comercialización independiente de energía eléctrica, incluyendo la autogeneración, cogeneración, generación y exportación eléctrica en el territorio nacional. El Poder Ejecutivo reglamentara la presente Ley en el plazo de 6 meses posteriores a la promulgación de Ia misma.

Policy: Law no. 2/2023 for fluorinated greenhouse gases.
Policy_Content: This Law aims to reduce emissions of fluorinated greenhouse gases, in order to achieve necessary environmental protection scopes. This Law defines: a) rules for import, export, processing, collection, recovery, recycling, destruction, dismantling, transportation, storage, placing on the market of fluorinated greenhouse gases and equipment that contains fluorinated greenhouse gases, or whose operation relies on such gases; b) the conditions for placing on the market of specific products and equipment that contain greenhouse gases fluorinated or whose operation relies on these gases; c) conditions for specific uses of fluorinated greenhouse gases; d) quantitative limits for placing hydrofluorocarbons on the market; e) requirements for licensing and authorization of entrepreneurs operating in the greenhouse gas market and dealing with fluorinated gasses and equipment containing these gases; f) requirements for training and certification of operators by accredited body for personal certification. The rules for import, export, processing, collection, recovery, recycling, destruction, dismantling, transportation, storage, placing on the market of fluorinated greenhouse gases and equipment that contains fluorinated greenhouse gases, or whose operation relies on such gases shall be implemented in accordance with the following principles: a) the principle of common, but differentiated responsibilities, according to which all parties of the Kigali Amendment of the Montreal Protocol, regardless of whether they are developing countries or not developed, take responsibility for the reduction of fluorinated greenhouse gases, according to the conditions of each country and within the new economic and political situation created; b) the principle of preventive care, according to which measures should be taken in the first place to anticipate, prevent or minimize human health and environmental problems deriving form the effects of harmful emissions, resulting or likely to result from human activity, which changes or deplete the ozone layer; c) the principle of efficiency, according to which policies and measures taken to reduce greenhouse gases fluoridation must be cost-effective, in such a way as to provide lowest global cost-benefit; d) the principle of sustainable development, according to which measures to protect the climate system from anthropogenic changes integrated into national development policies and programs should lead inti growing and sustainable economic and social development of the country; e) the principle of cooperation and national and international financing, according to which the efforts to reduced greenhouse gases can be done jointly and in coordination with other countries interested and, in addition to the state budget, to be supported by international or bilateral funding sources.

Policy: Recovery of Possession of Premises Given on Lease Act, No. 1 of 2023.
Policy_Content: This law regulates the procedure for the lessor to recover the premises given on lease from the lessee who does not vacate it at the end of the lease agreement. The lessor has to file a plaint with an affidavit, a draft decree nisi, and a copy of the lease agreement in the court. The court will issue a decree in favour of the lessor and serve it on the lessee, who can apply for leave to appear and show cause within fourteen days, but only after paying security for the arrears and costs. If the lessee does not apply or pay security, the court will make the decree nisi absolute and order the eviction of the lessee from the premises. If the lessee is granted leave, the court will hear and decide the case on its merits. The court can also award compensation to the lessor for any damage to the premises or any unpaid utility bills or service charges by the lessee. The Act applies to any premises given on lease by any lease agreement, and does not affect any other legal remedies available to either party.

Policy: Regional Law No. 12-RZ “On ensuring the fertility of agricultural land.”
Policy_Content: Fertility of agricultural land in the Republic of Ingushetia is unique and the most valuable natural resource forming the basis of agricultural production, and it should be guaranteed to use it in the interests of the regional population. This Regional Law establishes legal basis for state regulation of agricultural land fertility reproduction, except for horticulture and gardening agricultural land plots occupied by on-farm roads, communications, ameliorative protective forest plantations, waterbodies (including ponds formed by water-retaining structures on watercourses and used for the purposes implementation of pond aquaculture), as well as buildings, structures, used for production, storage and primary processing of agricultural products. Land owners, land users and land tenants have the right to: (a) carry out activities to restore agricultural land fertility; (b) conduct soil, geobotanical and other surveys of agricultural land; (c) submit to the federal state budget institution information about the use and condition of agricultural land; (d) receive in the prescribed manner from the state register of agricultural land information on agricultural land of which they are landowners, land users and land tenants; and (e) exercise other rights, unless their exercise is contrary to the laws and other regulatory legal acts of the Russian Federation.

Policy: Real Decreto Nº 3/2023 - Por el que se establecen los criterios técnicos-sanitarios de la calidad del agua de consumo, su control y suministro.
Policy_Content: El presente Real Decreto tiene por objeto establecer los criterios técnicos y sanitarios de las aguas de consumo y de su suministro y distribución, desde las masas de agua hasta el grifo del usuario, así como el control de su calidad, garantizando y mejorando su acceso, disponibilidad, salubridad y limpieza, con la finalidad de proteger la salud de las personas de los efectos adversos derivados de cualquier tipo de contaminación. El Real Decreto facilita el acceso al agua siguiendo lo indicado por Naciones Unidas en el derecho humano al agua y saneamiento en el Reino de España. También se establecen los requisitos de calidad del agua utilizada en la industria alimentaria para la fabricación de alimentos. Para tratar la preocupación sobre los posibles efectos de contaminantes emergentes en la salud humana se propone un mecanismo denominado «Lista de observación» que incluirá, entre otras, algunas sustancias identificadas como alteradores endocrinos. Conforme al Artículo 5º, el agua de consumo deberá ser salubre y limpia en el punto de cumplimiento. Un agua de consumo se considerará salubre y limpia cuando: a) Esté libre de microorganismo, parásito o sustancia, en una cantidad o concentración que pueda suponer un riesgo para la salud humana; b) Se cumpla, al menos, con los requisitos especificados en el anexo I de este Real Decreto. Las muestras de agua de consumo, se podrán calificar como: a) Apta para el consumo; y b) No apta para el consumo.

Policy: Genetic Resources Law.
Policy_Content: The purpose of this law is to regulate relationships related to the registration, preservation, protection, research, development, use, and benefit of genetic resources and traditional knowledge related to genetic resources. This Law applies to genetic resources derived from plants, animals, and microorganisms, and relationships related to traditional knowledge related to genetic resources. It shall not be applicable to human genetic resources. The State shall follow the following principles when using genetic resources and traditional knowledge related to genetic resources: (a) based on research and analysis, based on advanced techniques, technologies and innovations; (b) protection and appropriate use of genetic resources and traditional knowledge related to genetic resources; (c) openness and transparency; and (d) fair and equitable sharing of benefits. Genetic resources originating from the territory of Mongolia are the property of the state. Legal entities may be granted the right to study, conduct bioprospecting, and use traditional knowledge related to genetic resources under the conditions and procedures specified in this law. Discovery of traditional knowledge related to genetic resources, bioprospecting, use without registration in a database, transmission, sale, or benefiting from genetic resources is prohibited without a special license specified in this law. Plants, animals, and microorganisms containing genetic resources shall be protected by preserving and sustaining native habitats, domesticating them, replacing them, re-introducing them, cultivating them, and establishing gene banks, plants, and zoos. No special permit is required for the use of plants specified in the International Treaty on Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture to which Mongolia is a State Party. The license holder shall submit the following information and reports to the central government administration: (a) annual work report on the use of genetic resources and traditional knowledge related to genetic resources by February 10 of the following year; and (b) every time the information is entered into the database.
